title.zh: 卷七 齊本紀中第七: 顯祖文宣帝 廢帝 孝昭帝
title.en: Volume 7 Northern Qi Annals 2: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, Deposed Emperor, Emperor Xiaozhao
title.raw: 卷七 齊本紀中第七: 顯祖文宣帝 廢帝 孝昭帝 Volume 7 Northern Qi Annals 2: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, Deposed Emperor, Emperor Xiaozhao

sentences.zh: 顯祖文宣帝 廢帝 孝昭帝

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, Deposed Emperor, Emperor Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, the Deposed Emperor, and Emperor Xiaozhao.

sentences.zh: 顯祖文宣帝

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 顯祖文宣皇帝諱洋，字子進，神武第二子，文襄之母弟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, taboo name Yang, courtesy name Zijin, was the second son of Shenwu and the younger brother of Wenxiang by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, taboo name Yang, style name Zijin, was Shenwu's second son and Wenxiang's full younger brother.

sentences.zh: 武明太后初孕帝，每夜有赤光照室，太后私怪之。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wuming first carried the Emperor, each night red light filled the chamber, and the Empress Dowager privately wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wuming first conceived the Emperor, red light filled her chamber every night, and she privately marveled at the omen.

sentences.zh: 及產，命之曰侯尼于。

translations.literal: When he was born, she named him Hou Niyu.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth she named him Hou Niyu.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑言有相子也。

translations.literal: In Xianbei speech this meant "there is a son of noble aspect."
translations.idiomatic: In Xianbei this meant "a son of noble aspect."

sentences.zh: 以生於晉陽，一名晉陽樂。

translations.literal: Because he was born at Jinyang, he was also called Jinyang Le.
translations.idiomatic: Born at Jinyang, he was also called Jinyang Le.

sentences.zh: 時神武家徒壁立，后與親姻相對，共憂寒餒。

translations.literal: At that time Shenwu's household stood empty as a bare wall; the Empress and her kin faced one another, all fearing cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu's house was bare as a whitewashed wall; the Empress and her kin sat facing one another, dreading cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 帝生始數月，尚未能言，欻然曰：「得活。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had lived only a few months and could not yet speak, he suddenly said, "We shall live."
translations.idiomatic: Only months old and not yet able to speak, he suddenly said, "We shall live."

sentences.zh: 」太后及左右大驚，不敢言。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and those beside her were greatly startled and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and her attendants were stunned and dared say nothing.

sentences.zh: 及長，黑色，大頰兌下，鱗身重踝，瞻視審定，不好戲弄，深沈有大度。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was dark-skinned, with large cheeks and a heavy jaw, scaly skin and thick ankles; his gaze was steady and he did not care for play, being deep and possessed of great breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was dark of complexion, with heavy cheeks and jaw, scaly skin and thick ankles; his gaze was steady, he shunned childish games, and his nature was deep and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 晉陽有沙門，乍愚乍智，時人不測，呼為阿禿師。

translations.literal: At Jinyang there was a monk, at times foolish and at times wise, whom people could not fathom and called Master Atou.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang lived a monk, now dull and now sharp, whom none could read; they called him Master Atou.

sentences.zh: 太后見諸子焉，歷問祿位。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had him see all her sons and asked each in turn about his rank and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager brought him before her sons and asked each about his destined rank.

sentences.zh: 至帝，再三舉手指天而已，口無所言，見者異之。

translations.literal: When it came to the Emperor, he repeatedly raised his finger toward heaven and nothing more; those who saw this were struck as strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the Emperor he only lifted his finger to the sky again and again and said no word; the onlookers were astonished.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗從諸子過鳳陽門，有龍在上，唯神武與帝見之。

translations.literal: Shenwu once passed Fengyang Gate with his sons; a dragon appeared above, and only Shenwu and the Emperor saw it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shenwu passed Fengyang Gate with his sons; a dragon appeared overhead, seen by Shenwu and the Emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 內雖明敏，貌若不足，文襄每嗤之曰：「此人亦得富貴，相法亦何由可解。

translations.literal: Though inwardly keen and bright, in appearance he seemed deficient; Wenxiang often mocked him, saying, "That this man should attain wealth and rank—how can physiognomy be explained?"
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he was keen, yet he looked unremarkable; Wenxiang often jeered, "How can such a face ever win fortune? What use is physiognomy?"

sentences.zh: 」神武以帝貌陋，神彩不甚發揚，曾問以時事，帝略有所辨，儻語一事，必得事衷。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because the Emperor's looks were plain and his spirit did not seem to blaze forth, once questioned him on current affairs; the Emperor answered only in part, yet whenever he spoke of a matter he always hit the heart of it.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Emperor homely and outwardly dull, Shenwu once tested him on affairs of the day; he answered sparingly, yet each remark struck true.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令諸子，各使理亂絲，帝獨抽刀斬之，曰：「亂者須斬。

translations.literal: He also once had each son untangle a tangled skein of silk; the Emperor alone drew a blade and cut it, saying, "What is tangled must be cut."
translations.idiomatic: He once set each son to unravel tangled silk; the Emperor alone drew his knife and severed it, saying, "Tangles must be cut."

sentences.zh: 」神武以為然。

translations.literal: Shenwu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu agreed.

sentences.zh: 又各配兵四出，而使彭樂率甲騎偽攻之，文襄等怖撓，帝勒红與彭樂相格，樂免冑言情，猶禽之以獻。

translations.literal: He also assigned troops to each and sent them out in four directions, then had Peng Le lead armored horsemen in a feigned attack; Wenxiang and the others were frightened and shaken, but the Emperor drove his forces against Peng Le and fought him; Le removed his helmet and spoke from the heart, yet the Emperor still took him captive and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave each son troops and sent them forth, then had Peng Le feign an attack with armored cavalry; Wenxiang and the rest quailed, but the Emperor rallied his men, fought Peng Le face to face, and though Le bared his head and pleaded, still seized him and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 由是神武稱異之，謂長史薛琡曰：「此兒意識過吾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shenwu marveled at him and said to Chief Administrator Xue Ju, "This boy's mind surpasses mine."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu then wondered at him and told Chief Administrator Xue Ju, "This boy's understanding exceeds my own."

sentences.zh: 」琡亦私怪之。

translations.literal: Ju too privately found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Ju too was privately astonished.

sentences.zh: 幼時，師事范陽盧景裕，默識過人，未嘗有所自明，景裕不能測也。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Lu Jingyu of Fanyang; his silent memorization surpassed others, yet he never explained himself, and Jingyu could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied under Lu Jingyu of Fanyang; he remembered without effort and never showed his learning, so that Jingyu could not measure him.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，封太原郡公，累遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery and was promoted step by step to Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year two he received Taiyuan Commandery and rose through the ranks to Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後從文襄行過遼陽山，獨見天門開，餘無人見者。

translations.literal: Later, traveling with Wenxiang past Liaoyang Mountain, he alone saw the Gate of Heaven open; no one else saw it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, passing Liaoyang Mountain with Wenxiang, he alone saw Heaven's Gate open; none beside him saw it.

sentences.zh: 武定五年，神武崩，猶祕凶事，红情疑駭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wuding, Shenwu died; the death was still kept secret, and Yang was inwardly suspicious and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding year five Shenwu died; the death was still concealed, and Yang was inwardly fearful and unsettled.

sentences.zh: 帝雖內嬰巨痛，外若平常，人情頗安。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor bore great grief within, outwardly he seemed as usual, and people were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Though grief tore at him within, outwardly he seemed unchanged, and hearts grew steadier.

sentences.zh: 魏帝授帝尚書令、中書監、京畿大都督。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor appointed the Emperor Director of the Masters of Writing, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor made him Director of the Masters of Writing, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，文襄遇賊，帝在城東雙堂，事出倉卒，內外震駭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, Wenxiang was set upon by assassins; the Emperor was at Shuang Hall east of the city, and the affair came in sudden haste; within and without all were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, eighth month, Wenxiang fell to assassins; the Emperor was at Shuang Hall east of the city; the blow came without warning and panic seized court and camp.

sentences.zh: 帝神色不變，指麾部分，自臠斬戝賊而漆其首，祕不發喪。

translations.literal: The Emperor's expression did not change; he directed the disposition of forces, personally cut the assassin to pieces and lacquered the head, and kept the death secret.
translations.idiomatic: His face never changed; he deployed the troops, himself hacked the assassin apart and lacquered the head, and hid the death.

sentences.zh: 徐言奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。

translations.literal: He said calmly that the slave Xu had rebelled and the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave.
translations.idiomatic: Calmly he said the slave Xu had rebelled and the Grand General was hurt, but not gravely.

sentences.zh: 當時內外，莫不驚異。

translations.literal: At the time, within and without, none failed to marvel.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp alike were astonished.

sentences.zh: 乃諷魏朝立皇太子，因以大赦。

translations.literal: He then prompted the Wei court to install the crown prince and thereby proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved the Wei court to install the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乃赴晉陽總庶政。

translations.literal: Then he went to Jinyang to take overall charge of government.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to Jinyang to govern all affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝內雖明察，外若不了，老臣宿將皆輕帝。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor was inwardly keen and perceptive, outwardly he seemed not to understand; old ministers and veteran generals all looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Keen within yet seeming dull without, he was underestimated by old ministers and seasoned generals.

sentences.zh: 於是帝推誠接下，務從寬厚，事有不便者咸蠲省焉，戝情始服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor treated subordinates with sincerity, striving for leniency; whatever was inconvenient he abolished or reduced, and the soldiers' hearts came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then dealt sincerely with those below, favoring leniency, repealed what burdened the people, and won the soldiers' trust.

sentences.zh: 八年正月辛酉，魏帝為文襄舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou of the first month of the eighth year, the Wei Emperor held mourning for Wenxiang at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou of the first month in year eight the Wei Emperor mourned Wenxiang at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔進帝位使持節、丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺、齊郡王，食邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen an edict advanced the Emperor to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commissioner, Prince of Qi Commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen an edict raised him to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commissioner, and Prince of Qi Commandery, with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 三月庚申，又進封齊王，食冀州之勃海、長樂、安德、武邑、瀛州之河間五郡，邑十萬戶。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen of the third month he was further advanced to Prince of Qi, with the five commanderies of Bohai and Changle in Ji Province, Ande and Wuyi, and Hejian in Ying Province, ten thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the third month he became Prince of Qi, receiving Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Ji Province and Hejian in Ying Province—ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帝自居晉陽，寢室每夜有光如晝。

translations.literal: While the Emperor resided at Jinyang, his sleeping chamber each night had light bright as day.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang his bedchamber shone each night bright as noon.

sentences.zh: 既為王，夢人以筆點己額。

translations.literal: After he became prince, he dreamed that a man dotted his forehead with a brush.
translations.idiomatic: Once prince, he dreamed a man marked his brow with a brush.

sentences.zh: 旦日，以語館客王曇哲，曰：「吾其退乎？

translations.literal: At dawn he told his guest Wang Tanzi, saying, "Am I to withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his guest Wang Tanzi, "Am I to step back?"

sentences.zh: 」曇哲拜賀曰：「王上加點為主，當進也。」

translations.literal: Tanzi bowed in congratulation and said, "When the character for prince receives a dot it becomes the character for lord—you are to advance."
translations.idiomatic: Tanzi bowed and said, "Add a dot to the character for prince and it becomes lord—you are to rise."

sentences.zh: 五月辛亥，帝如鄴。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai of the fifth month the Emperor went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai of the fifth month he went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 光州獲九尾狐以獻。

translations.literal: Guang Province presented a nine-tailed fox as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Province sent up a nine-tailed fox.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏帝遣兼太尉彭城王韶、司空潘相樂奉冊，進帝位相國，總百揆，以冀州之勃海、長樂、安德、武邑、瀛州之河間、高陽、章武、定州之中山、常山、博陵十郡，邑二十萬戶，加九錫殊禮，齊王如故。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin the Wei Emperor sent Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue to present the investiture, advancing the Emperor to Prime Minister with overall charge of all affairs, with the ten commanderies of Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Ji Province, Hejian, Gaoyang, and Zhangwu in Ying Province, and Zhongshan, Changshan, and Boling in Ding Province, two hundred thousand households, plus the Nine Bestowals and extraordinary honors, remaining Prince of Qi as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Wei Emperor sent Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue with the seal, making him Prime Minister over all affairs, granting ten commanderies and two hundred thousand households, the Nine Bestowals, and the title Prince of Qi unchanged.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏帝遜位別宮，又使兼太尉彭城王韶、兼司空敬顯侊奉冊禪位，致璽書於帝，并奉皇帝璽綬，禪代之禮，一依唐、虞、漢、魏故事。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen the Wei Emperor abdicated to a separate palace, and again sent Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Concurrent Minister of Works Jing Xianghong to present the abdication seal, deliver the imperial missive to the Emperor, and together present the imperial seal and cord; the rites of abdication followed entirely the precedents of Tang, Yu, Han, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Wei Emperor retired to a separate palace and again sent Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Concurrent Minister of Works Jing Xianghong with the abdication seal, the imperial letter, and the imperial seal and cord, following the rites of Tang, Yu, Han, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝累表固辭，詔不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly memorialized firmly declining; the edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again and again to refuse; the edict would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書令高隆之率百僚勸進。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi led the hundred officials in urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi then led the hundred officials in urging acceptance.

sentences.zh: 天保元年夏五月戊午，皇帝即位於南郊，升壇，柴燎告天。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the fifth month in the first year of Tianbao, the Emperor took the throne at the Southern Altar, ascended the mound, and reported to Heaven with burnt offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of the fifth month, Tianbao year one, he ascended the throne at the Southern Altar, mounted the mound, and offered burnt sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是日，鄴下獲赤雀，獻于郊所。

translations.literal: That day a vermilion sparrow was caught below Ye and presented at the altar.
translations.idiomatic: That day a vermilion sparrow was taken below Ye and offered at the altar.

sentences.zh: 事畢還宮，御太極前殿，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished he returned to the palace, took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Pole, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended he returned, sat in the Hall of Supreme Pole, pardoned the realm, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 百官進兩大階，六州緣邊職人三大階。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were advanced two full ranks; frontier officials of the six provinces, three full ranks.
translations.idiomatic: All officials rose two full ranks; frontier officials of six provinces, three.

sentences.zh: 自魏孝莊已後，百官絕祿，至是復給焉。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei, officials had received no salary; from this time salaries were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei Emperor Xiaozhuang officials had gone without pay; now pay was restored.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔封魏帝為中山王。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei an edict enfeoffed the Wei Emperor as Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict made the Wei Emperor Prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇祖文穆王為文穆皇帝，皇祖妣為文穆皇后，皇考獻武王為獻武皇帝，皇兄文襄王為文襄皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his imperial grandfather King Wenmu as Emperor Wenmu and his imperial grandmother as Empress Wenmu; his imperial father King Xianwu as Emperor Xianwu; his elder brother King Wenxiang as Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his grandfather King Wenmu to Emperor Wenmu and his grandmother to Empress Wenmu; his father King Xianwu to Emperor Xianwu; his brother King Wenxiang to Emperor Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 命有司議祖宗以聞。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials to deliberate on the imperial ancestors and report.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the officials to settle the imperial temple and report.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，尊王太后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou he honored the Queen Dowager as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he raised the Queen Dowager to Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，降魏朝封爵各有差；

translations.literal: On the day yichou he reduced the ranks and fiefs of the Wei court, each according to its measure;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he lowered Wei court ranks and fiefs by degree;

sentences.zh: [一]其信都從義，及宣力霸朝者，又西來人，并武定六年以來南來投化者，不在降限。

translations.literal: Those of Xindu who followed righteousness, those who had exerted strength for the hegemonic court, men who had come from the west, and those who had submitted from the south since the sixth year of Wuding were not within the scope of reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt from reduction were men of Xindu who had kept faith, those who had served the founding court, newcomers from the west, and southerners who had submitted since Wuding year six.

sentences.zh: 辛未，遣大使於四方觀察風俗，問人疾苦。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei he sent great envoys to the four quarters to observe local customs and inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he sent great envoys abroad to observe customs and ask after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遷神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu the spirit tablets were moved to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the spirit tablets entered the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，詔改封崇聖侯孔長為恭聖侯，邑一百戶，以奉孔子祀，并下魯郡，以時修葺廟宇。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi of the sixth month an edict changed the enfeoffment of Venerable Sage Kong Chang to Reverent Sage Kong Chang, with a fief of one hundred households for the sacrifice to Confucius, and ordered Lu Commandery to repair the temple in season.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the sixth month he changed Venerable Sage Kong Chang to Reverent Sage Kong Chang, with one hundred households for Confucian rites, and ordered Lu Commandery to keep the temple in repair.

sentences.zh: 又詔：吉凶車服制度，各為等差，具立條式，使儉而獲中。

translations.literal: Another edict: systems for auspicious and inauspicious occasions, carriages and dress were each graded by rank, with detailed regulations set forth so that thrift might yet hit the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict graded carriages, dress, and rites for joy and mourning by rank, setting rules so that thrift would still be fitting.

sentences.zh: 分遣使人致祭於五岳、四瀆，其堯祠、舜廟下及孔父、老君等載於祀典者，咸秩罔遺。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent separately to offer sacrifice at the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers; shrines to Yao, temples to Shun, and those recorded in the canon such as Kong the Father and Lord Lao were all included in the sacrificial order without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to sacrifice at the Five Peaks and Four Rivers; shrines to Yao, temples to Shun, Kong the Father, Lord Lao, and all canonized worthies received their due rites.

sentences.zh: 又詔：冀州之勃海、長樂二郡，先帝始封之國，義旗初起之地；

translations.literal: Another edict: Bohai and Changle commanderies in Ji Province were the lands first enfeoffed to the Former Emperor and the place where the righteous banner first rose;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict: Bohai and Changle in Ji Province were the Former Emperor's first fief and the birthplace of the righteous cause;

sentences.zh: 并州之太原、青州之齊郡，霸朝所在，王命是基。

translations.literal: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province were where the hegemonic court stood and where the royal mandate took root.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province were the seat of the founding court and the root of the royal mandate.

sentences.zh: 君子有作，貴不忘本，齊郡、勃海，可並復一年，長樂復二年，太原復三年。

translations.literal: When a gentleman acts, he honors his origins; Qi Commandery and Bohai were each granted one year's remission, Changle two years, and Taiyuan three years.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman does not forget his origins: Qi Commandery and Bohai received one year's tax remission, Changle two, Taiyuan three.

sentences.zh: 壬午，詔故太傅孫騰、故太保尉景、故大司馬婁昭、故司徒高敖曹、故尚書左僕射慕容紹宗、故領軍万俟干、故定州刺史段榮、故御史中尉劉貴、故御史中尉竇泰、故殷州刺史劉豐、故濟州刺史蔡侊等，並左右先帝，經贊皇基，或不幸早殂，或隕身王事，可遣使者就墓致祭，并撫問妻子。

translations.literal: On the day renwu an edict addressed the late Grand Tutor Sun Teng, late Grand Mentor Wei Jing, late Grand Marshal Lou Zhao, late Minister of Works Gao Aocao, late Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Murong Shaozong, late Commander of the Guard Wan Qigan, late Inspector of Ding Province Duan Rong, late Imperial Censor Liu Gui, late Imperial Censor Dou Tai, late Inspector of Yin Province Liu Feng, late Inspector of Ji Province Cai Hong, and others—all had stood at the Former Emperor's side and helped establish the imperial foundation; some had died untimely, some had fallen in the king's service; envoys were to be sent to their tombs to offer sacrifice and to comfort their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu an edict named the late Sun Teng, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Gao Aocao, Murong Shaozong, Wan Qigan, Duan Rong, Liu Gui, Dou Tai, Liu Feng, Cai Hong, and others who had served the Former Emperor and built the throne—some dying young, some in battle—and ordered envoys to sacrifice at their tombs and comfort their families.

sentences.zh: 又詔封宗室，太尉高岳為清河王，太保高隆之為平原王，開府儀同三司高歸彥為平秦王，徐州刺史高思宗為上洛王，營州刺史高長弼為廣武王，兼武纫將軍高普為武興王，兼武纫將軍高子瑗為平昌王，兼北中郎將高顯國為襄樂王，前太子庶子高叡為趙郡王，揚州縣開國公高孝緒為脩城王。

translations.literal: Another edict enfeoffed members of the imperial clan: Grand Commandant Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Grand Mentor Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Inspector of Xu Province Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Inspector of Ying Province Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Concurrent General of Martial Arrows Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Concurrent General of Martial Arrows Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Concurrent North Commander of the Gentlemen Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, former Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Gao Rui as Prince of Zhao Commandery, and Yangzhou County Duke Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed the clan: Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, Gao Rui as Prince of Zhao Commandery, and Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 又詔封功臣，太師厙狄干為章武王，大司馬斛律金為咸陽王，并州刺史賀拔仁為安定王，殷州刺史韓軌為安德王，瀛州刺史可朱渾道元為扶風王，司徒公彭樂為陳留王，司空公潘相樂為河東王。

translations.literal: Another edict enfeoffed meritorious ministers: Grand Preceptor Kudie Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Grand Marshal Hulu Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Inspector of Bing Province Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Inspector of Yin Province Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Inspector of Ying Province Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Minister of Works Duke Peng Le as Prince of Chenliu, and Minister of Works Duke Pan Xiangyue as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed the great ministers: Kudie Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Hulu Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Peng Le as Prince of Chenliu, and Pan Xiangyue as Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔封諸弟，青州刺史浚為永安王，尚書左僕射淹為平陽王，定州刺史浟為彭城王，儀同三司演為常山王，冀州刺史渙為上黨王，儀同三司淯為襄城王，儀同三司湛為長廣王，湝為任城王，湜為高陽王，濟為博陵王，凝為新平王，潤為馮翊王，洽為漢陽王。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei an edict enfeoffed the younger brothers: Inspector of Qing Province Jun as Prince of Yong'an, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Yan as Prince of Pingyang, Inspector of Ding Province You as Prince of Pengcheng, Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Yan as Prince of Changshan, Inspector of Ji Province Huan as Prince of Shangdang, Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng, Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Zhan as Prince of Changgang, Sheng as Prince of Rencheng, Shi as Prince of Gaoyang, Ji as Prince of Boling, Ning as Prince of Xinping, Run as Prince of Fengyi, and Qia as Prince of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he enfeoffed his brothers: Jun as Prince of Yong'an, Yan as Prince of Pingyang, You as Prince of Pengcheng, Yan as Prince of Changshan, Huan as Prince of Shangdang, Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng, Zhan as Prince of Changgang, Sheng as Prince of Rencheng, Shi as Prince of Gaoyang, Ji as Prince of Boling, Ning as Prince of Xinping, Run as Prince of Fengyi, and Qia as Prince of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔立王子殷為皇太子，王后李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai an edict installed the prince's son Yin as crown prince and the queen, Lady Li, as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he made Prince Yin crown prince and Lady Li empress.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔以太師厙狄干為太宰，司徒彭樂為太尉，司空潘相樂為司徒，開府儀同三司司馬子如為司空。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin an edict appointed Grand Preceptor Kudie Gan as Grand Mentor, Minister of Works Peng Le as Grand Commandant, Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue as Minister of Works, and Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Sima Ziru as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he made Kudie Gan Grand Mentor, Peng Le Grand Commandant, Pan Xiangyue Minister of Works, and Sima Ziru Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以皇太子初入東宮，赦畿內及并州死罪已下，降餘州死罪己下囚。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, because the crown prince had first entered the Eastern Palace, he pardoned within the capital region and Bing Province all prisoners down from capital crimes, and in the remaining provinces all down from capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, when the crown prince first entered the Eastern Palace, he pardoned capital-region and Bing prisoners down from capital crimes and the rest of the provinces down from capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛亥，尊文襄妃元氏為文襄皇后，宮曰靜德。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day xinhai, he honored Wenxiang's consort Lady Yuan as Empress Wenxiang; her palace was called Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on xinhai, he raised Wenxiang's consort Lady Yuan to Empress Wenxiang; her palace was Jingde.

sentences.zh: 又封文襄子孝琬為河間王，孝瑜為河南王。

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed Wenxiang's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian and Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Wenxiang's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian and Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以尚書令、平原王隆之為錄尚書事，[二]尚書左僕射、平陽王淹為尚書令，改御史中尉還為中丞。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi, as Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingyang Yan, as Director of the Masters of Writing; and restored the Imperial Censor to the title Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he made Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingyang Yan Director of the Masters of Writing, and restored the Imperial Censor to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 詔魏御府所有珍奇雜綵常所不給人者，悉送內後園，以供七日宴賜。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all rare treasures and miscellaneous silks in the Wei imperial storehouse that were not ordinarily given to men be sent to the inner rear garden to supply seven days of feasting and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent every rare treasure and special silk from the Wei storehouse, ordinarily withheld from grant, to the inner garden for seven days of feasting and gifts.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔郡國修立黌序，廣延髦俊，敦述儒風。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered commanderies and kingdoms to establish schools, broadly recruit eminent scholars, and earnestly carry forward Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he ordered commanderies and kingdoms to build schools, gather eminent scholars, and advance Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 其國子學生，亦依舊銓補。

translations.literal: Students of the Directorate of Education were also appointed by the former rules of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students were also appointed under the old selection rules.

sentences.zh: 往者文襄皇帝所運蔡邕石經五十二枚，移置學館，依次修立。

translations.literal: The fifty-two stone classics of Cai Yong that Former Emperor Wenxiang had transported were moved to the academy and set up in order for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The fifty-two Cai Yong stone classics Wenxiang had moved were placed in the academy and restored in order.

sentences.zh: 又詔求直言正諫之士，待以不次；

translations.literal: Another edict sought men who spoke blunt truth and offered straight remonstrance, to be treated with extraordinary promotion;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict sought blunt speakers and straight remonstrators for preferment beyond the usual order;

sentences.zh: 命牧人之官，廣勸農桑。

translations.literal: pastoral officials were ordered broadly to encourage agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered pastoral officials to urge farming and mulberry cultivation.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔曰：「朕以虛薄，嗣弘王業，思所以贊揚盛績，播之萬古。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin an edict said, "We, being meager and slight, have succeeded to the great royal enterprise and think how to extol the flourishing achievement and spread it through ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict read, "We, thin in virtue, have inherited the great enterprise and wish to praise its glory for ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 雖史官執筆，有聞無墜，猶恐緒言遺美，時或未書。

translations.literal: Though the historiographers hold the brush and what is heard is not lost, we still fear that fine words and deeds left unrecorded at the time may be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Though scribes record what they hear, we fear fine deeds and words may still be lost if not written in time.

sentences.zh: 在位王公、文武大小，降及庶人，爰至僧徒，或親奉音旨，或承傳旁說，凡可載之文籍，悉條封上。

translations.literal: From enthroned princes and dukes, civil and military great and small, down to commoners, even to monks—whoever has personally received our words or heard them at second hand—whatever writings can be recorded, let all be listed and sealed and sent up.
translations.idiomatic: From princes, dukes, and officers high and low to commoners and monks—any who heard our words directly or indirectly—let all recordable writings be listed, sealed, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，詔曰：「魏世議定麟趾格，遂為通制，官司施用，猶未盡善。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu an edict said, "In Wei times the Linzhi Code was settled and became the universal standard; yet in official use it is still not fully perfected.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu an edict read, "Wei's Linzhi Code became the universal law, yet officials still find it imperfect.

sentences.zh: 戝官可更論討新令。

translations.literal: Officials may further discuss and draft a new code.
translations.idiomatic: Let officials draft a new code.

sentences.zh: 未成之間，仍以舊格從事。」

translations.literal: Until it is complete, the old code shall still govern."
translations.idiomatic: Until then the old code remains in force."

sentences.zh: 九月癸丑，以領東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高麗王成為使持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉，王、公如故。

translations.literal: On the day guichou he appointed Commander of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong Commandery, King of Goguryeo Gwang as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, General of Fast Cavalry, and Commander of the Guard of the Eastern Yi; his kingly and ducal titles remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he confirmed Goguryeo King Gwang as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, General of Fast Cavalry, and Commander of the Eastern Yi, with kingly and ducal titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔以梁侍中、使持節、假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、承制邵陵王蕭綸為梁王。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao an edict enfeoffed Liang Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Acting Golden Battle-Axe, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand General, and Holder of Imperial Authority Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he enfeoffed Liang Palace Attendant Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun, acting Golden Battle-Axe and Grand General, as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 庚午，幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu he visited Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太子入居涼風堂，監國。

translations.literal: That day the crown prince entered Cool Wind Hall to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince entered Cool Wind Hall to govern in his stead.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己卯，法駕，御金輅，入晉陽宮，朝皇太后於內殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the day jimao, with the imperial carriage and escort he rode the golden chariot, entered Jinyang Palace, and attended upon the Empress Dowager in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jimao, he rode the golden chariot into Jinyang Palace and attended the Empress Dowager in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，曲赦并州太原郡晉陽縣及相國府四獄囚。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he granted a partial amnesty to prisoners in the four prisons of Taiyuan Commandery, Jinyang County, and the Prime Minister's office in Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he pardoned prisoners in the four prisons of Taiyuan, Jinyang County, and the Prime Minister's office.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以特進元韶為尚書左僕射，[三]并州刺史段韶為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou he appointed Special Court Advisor Yuan Shao as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Bing Province Duan Shao as Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he made Yuan Shao Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Duan Shao of Bing Province Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，罷相國府，留騎兵、外兵曹，各立一省，別掌機密。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he abolished the Prime Minister's office, retaining the Bureaus of Cavalry and External Military Affairs, each established as a separate department to handle secrets.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he dissolved the Prime Minister's office but kept separate Bureaus of Cavalry and External Military Affairs for confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 十一月，周文帝帥師至陝城，分騎北度至建州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wen of Zhou led his army to Shancheng and sent cavalry north in detachments as far as Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhou's Wen led troops to Shancheng and sent cavalry north to Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，梁湘東王蕭繹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong of Liang, sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Liang's Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，帝親戎出次城東，周文帝見軍容嚴盛，歎曰：「高歡不死矣！

translations.literal: On the day bingyin the Emperor personally took the field and encamped east of the city; Wen of Zhou saw the army's array stern and full, sighed, and said, "Gao Huan is not dead after all!
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Emperor took the field and camped east of the city; Zhou's Wen saw the army's stern array and sighed, "Gao Huan is not dead!

sentences.zh: 」遂班師。

translations.literal: Then he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Then he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛丑，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou of the twelfth month the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou of the twelfth month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗、蠕蠕、吐谷渾、庫莫奚並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Goguryeo, Rouran, Tuyuhun, and Kumo Xi all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Goguryeo, Rouran, Tuyuhun, and Kumo Xi all sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丁未，梁湘東王蕭繹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on the day dingwei, Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong of Liang, sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year two, on dingwei, Liang's Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，祀圓丘，以神武皇帝配。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he sacrificed at the Round Mound, with Emperor Shenwu as associate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he sacrificed at the Round Mound with Emperor Shenwu as associate.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，親耕籍田。

translations.literal: On the day guihai he personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he plowed the sacred field himself.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，享太廟。

translations.literal: On the day yichou he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 二月壬辰，太尉彭樂謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the second month Grand Commandant Peng Le plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen of the second month Grand Commandant Peng Le rebelled and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 三月丙午，襄城王淯薨。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu Prince of Xiangcheng Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Prince of Xiangcheng Yu died.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔梁承制湘東王繹為梁使持節、假黃鉞、相國，建梁臺，總百揆、承制梁王。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei an edict made Liang Holder of Imperial Authority Prince of Xiangdong Yi Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Acting Golden Battle-Axe, and Prime Minister, established the Liang Terrace, with overall charge of all affairs and the title Prince of Liang with imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict made Liang's Prince of Xiangdong Yi Prime Minister with Acting Golden Battle-Axe, established the Liang Terrace, and granted him overall authority as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，司空司馬子如坐事免。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen Minister of Works Sima Ziru was removed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Minister of Works Sima Ziru was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 是月，梁交、梁、義、新四州刺史，各以地內附。

translations.literal: That month the four provincial governors of Jiao, Liang, Yi, and Xin in Liang each submitted their territories.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liang's governors of Jiao, Liang, Yi, and Xin each submitted their territories.

sentences.zh: 西魏文帝崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Western Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei's Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬辰，梁王蕭繹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the day renchen, Prince of Liang Xiao Yi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on renchen, Prince of Liang Xiao Yi sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午，以前司空司馬子如為太尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengwu, former Minister of Works Sima Ziru was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengwu, former Minister of Works Sima Ziru became Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，改顯陽殿還為昭陽殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day jimao, Xianyang Hall was restored to its former name Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jimao, Xianyang Hall was renamed Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，改殷州為趙州以避太子之諱。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao Yin Province was changed to Zhao Province to avoid the crown prince's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Yin Province became Zhao Province to avoid the crown prince's taboo.

sentences.zh: 是月，侯景廢梁簡文帝，立蕭棟為主。

translations.literal: That month Hou Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen of Liang and installed Xiao Dong as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: That month Hou Jing deposed Liang's Emperor Jianwen and set up Xiao Dong.

sentences.zh: [四]九月壬申，免諸伎作屯牧雜色役隸之徒為白戶。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the ninth month all performers, corvée laborers, herdsmen, and miscellaneous bond servants were freed as common households.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen of the ninth month performers, corvée workers, herdsmen, and bond servants were freed as common households.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，行幸趙、定二州，因至晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guisi he traveled to Zhao and Ding provinces and then went on to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he visited Zhao and Ding provinces and continued to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊申，起宣光、建始、嘉福、仁壽諸殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the day wushen, he began construction of the Xuanguang, Jianshi, Jiafu, and Renshou halls.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on wushen, he began the Xuanguang, Jianshi, Jiafu, and Renshou halls.

sentences.zh: 庚申，蕭繹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen Xiao Yi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Xiao Yi sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，文襄皇帝神主入于廟。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao the spirit tablet of Emperor Wenxiang entered the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Emperor Wenxiang's spirit tablet entered the temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月，侯景廢梁主棟，僭即偽位於建鄴，自稱曰漢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Hou Jing deposed Liang ruler Dong, usurped the throne at Jiankang, and styled himself Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hou Jing deposed Dong, seized the throne at Jiankang, and called his state Han.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中山王殂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Zhongshan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Prince of Zhongshan died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蠕蠕、室韋、高麗並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Rouran, Shiwei, and Goguryeo all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Rouran, Shiwei, and Goguryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丙申，帝親討庫莫奚於代郡，大破之，以其口配山東為百姓。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, on the day bingshen, the Emperor personally attacked the Kumo Xi in Dai Commandery, routed them utterly, and distributed their people to Shandong as common households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, on bingshen, he attacked the Kumo Xi in Dai Commandery, crushed them, and settled their people in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二月，蠕蠕主阿那镬為突厥所破，镬自殺。

translations.literal: In the second month the Rouran khan Anagui was broken by the Turks; Anagui killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Rouran khan Anagui was broken by the Turks and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 其太子菴羅辰及镬從弟登注俟利、[五]登注子庫提並擁红來奔。

translations.literal: His crown prince Yanluochen and Anagui's younger cousin Dengzhu Houli and Dengzhu's son Kuti all led their tribes in flight to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Yanluochen, Anagui's cousin Dengzhu Houli, and Dengzhu's son Kuti led their tribes to surrender.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕餘红立注次子鐵伐為主。

translations.literal: The Rouran remnant installed Dengzhu's second son Tiefa as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran survivors made Dengzhu's son Tiefa khan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，契丹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou the Khitan sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Khitan sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三月戊子，詔清河王岳、司徒潘相樂、行臺辛術帥師南伐。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi an edict ordered Prince of Qinghe Yue, Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue, and Commissioner Xin Shu to lead armies south.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an edict sent Prince of Qinghe Yue, Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue, and Commissioner Xin Shu south with armies.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔進梁王蕭繹為梁主。

translations.literal: On the day guisi an edict advanced Prince of Liang Xiao Yi to ruler of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi an edict made Prince of Liang Xiao Yi ruler of Liang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，東南道行臺辛術於廣陵送傳國八璽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the day renshen, Commissioner Xin Shu of the Southeastern Circuit at Guangling presented the eight imperial seals of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on renshen, Commissioner Xin Shu of the Southeastern Circuit presented the eight imperial seals at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以吏部尚書楊愔為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen Director of Personnel Yang Yin was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Director of Personnel Yang Yin became Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六月已亥，清河王岳等班師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jihai, Prince of Qinghe Yue and the others returned their armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jihai, Prince of Qinghe Yue and the rest returned.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day yimao the imperial carriage visited Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，西魏廢帝元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Western Wei Deposed Emperor year one.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月丙子，山胡圍離石戍，帝親討之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, on the day bingzi, the Shanhu besieged Lishi garrison; the Emperor personally attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, first month, on bingzi, the Shanhu besieged Lishi; the Emperor attacked in person.

sentences.zh: 未至而逃，因巡三堆戍，大狩而旋。

translations.literal: Before he arrived they fled; he then inspected the three-stack garrisons, held a great hunt, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They fled before he arrived; he inspected the three-stack garrisons, hunted greatly, and returned.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，庫莫奚遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin the Kumo Xi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Kumo Xi sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 自魏末用永安錢，又有數品，皆輕濫，己丑，鑄新錢，文曰常平五銖。

translations.literal: Since the end of Wei the Yongan coin had been used, with several types, all debased; on the day jichou new coin was cast, inscribed Changping Five Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Wei the debased Yongan coin had circulated; on jichou new coin was cast reading Changping Five Zhu.

sentences.zh: 二月，送蠕蠕鐵伐父登注及子庫提還北。

translations.literal: In the second month Tiefa's father Dengzhu and son Kuti of Rouran were sent back north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Rouran's Dengzhu and Kuti were sent north.

sentences.zh: 鐵伐尋為契丹所殺，國人復立登注為主，仍為其大人阿富提等所殺，國人復立庫提為主。

translations.literal: Tiefa was soon killed by the Khitan; the people again installed Dengzhu as khan, but he was again killed by the great man Afuti and others; the people again installed Kuti as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Tiefa was soon killed by the Khitan; the people made Dengzhu khan, then Afuti killed him; they made Kuti khan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 戊午，西南有大聲如雷。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu a great sound like thunder came from the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu a thunderous sound rose in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午，校獵於林慮山。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengwu, he held a hunting review on Mount Linlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengwu, he hunted on Mount Linlu.

sentences.zh: 戊子，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，章武王厙狄干薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiachen, Prince of Zhangwu Kudie Gan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Prince of Zhangwu Kudie Gan died.

sentences.zh: 秋，北巡冀、定、幽、安，仍北討契丹。

translations.literal: In autumn he toured north through Ji, Ding, You, and An, then continued north to attack the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he toured Ji, Ding, You, and An, then marched north against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁酉，車駕至平州，遂西道趣長塹。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the day dingyou, the imperial carriage reached Ping Province, then took the western road toward the Long Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on dingyou, he reached Ping Province and turned west toward the Long Rampart.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝步踰山嶺，為士卒先，指麾奮擊，大破契丹。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen the Emperor walked over mountain ridges ahead of the soldiers, directed the assault, and routed the Khitan utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he crossed the ridges ahead of his men, directed the charge, and broke the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是行也，帝露頭袒身，晝夜不息，行千餘里，唯食肉飲水，氣色彌厲。

translations.literal: On this campaign the Emperor went bareheaded and bare-chested, day and night without rest, marching more than a thousand li, eating only meat and drinking only water, his vigor growing fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: On this march he went bareheaded and bare-chested, never resting day or night, covering a thousand li on meat and water alone, his vigor only sharpening.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，登碣石山，臨滄海。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi he ascended Jieshi Mountain and looked out over the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he climbed Jieshi Mountain and gazed on the sea.

sentences.zh: 十一月己未，帝自平州還，遂如晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the eleventh month the Emperor returned from Ping Province and went on to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of the eleventh month he returned from Ping Province to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬寅，梁人來聘。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day renyin, men of Liang came on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renyin, Liang envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，突厥復攻蠕蠕，蠕蠕舉國來奔。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the twelfth month the Turks again attacked Rouran, and Rouran came in flight with the whole nation.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of the twelfth month the Turks attacked Rouran again and all Rouran fled to surrender.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝北討突厥，迎納蠕蠕。

translations.literal: On the day guihai the Emperor marched north against the Turks to welcome and receive the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he marched north against the Turks to receive the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 乃廢其主庫提，立阿那瓌子菴羅辰為主，置之馬邑川。

translations.literal: He then deposed their khan Kuti, installed Anagui's son Yanluochen as khan, and settled him at Mayi River.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Kuti, installed Anagui's son Yanluochen as khan, and settled him on the Mayi River.

sentences.zh: 追突厥於朔方，突厥請降，許之而還。

translations.literal: Pursuing the Turks to Shuofang, the Turks requested surrender; he granted it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Turks to Shuofang; they surrendered and he returned.

sentences.zh: 自是貢獻相繼。

translations.literal: From this time tribute followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute came in steady stream.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月癸丑，帝討山胡大破之，男子十二已上皆斬，女子及幼弱以賞軍士，遂平石樓。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on the day guichou, the Emperor attacked the Shanhu and routed them; all males twelve and above were beheaded, women and the young were given as rewards to the soldiers, and Shilou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, first month, on guichou, he crushed the Shanhu, beheaded all males twelve and up, gave women and children to the troops, and pacified Shilou.

sentences.zh: 石樓絕險，自魏代所不能至。

translations.literal: Shilou was utterly perilous; since the Wei dynasty none had reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilou was impregnable; since Wei none had taken it.

sentences.zh: 於是遠近山胡，莫不懾伏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shanhu near and far were all cowed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shanhu far and near submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 是役也，有都督戰傷，其什長路暉禮不能救，帝命刳其五藏，使九人分食之，肉及穢惡皆盡。

translations.literal: On this campaign a commander was wounded in battle; his squad leader Lu Huili could not rescue him; the Emperor ordered his five viscera cut out and nine men to eat them in shares until flesh and filth were all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign a commander was wounded; squad leader Lu Huili failed to save him; the Emperor had his entrails cut out and divided among nine men until all was eaten.

sentences.zh: 自是始行威虐。

translations.literal: From this time he began to practice cruel severity.
translations.idiomatic: From this he began his reign of terror.

sentences.zh: 是月，周文帝廢西魏帝而立齊王廓，是為恭帝。

translations.literal: That month Wen of Zhou deposed the Western Wei emperor and installed Prince of Qi Kuo, who is known as Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhou's Wen deposed Western Wei's emperor and set up Prince of Qi Kuo as Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 三月，蠕蠕菴羅辰叛，帝親討大破之，辰父子北遁。

translations.literal: In the third month Yanluochen of Rouran rebelled; the Emperor personally attacked and routed them utterly; Chen and his son fled north.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Rouran's Yanluochen rebelled; the Emperor crushed them in person; Chen and his son fled north.

sentences.zh: 太保賀拔仁坐違緩，拔其髮，免為庶人，使負炭輸晉陽宮。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Heba Ren was punished for tardiness; his hair was pulled out, he was reduced to commoner, and made to carry charcoal to Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Heba Ren was punished for delay; his hair was torn out, he was made a commoner, and set to carry charcoal to Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，蠕蠕寇肆州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Rouran raided Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Rouran raided Si Province.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，帝自晉陽討之，至恒州。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi the Emperor marched from Jinyang against them and reached Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he marched from Jinyang against them to Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 時虜騎散走，大軍已還，帝帥麾下二千餘騎為殿，夜宿黃瓜堆。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian horsemen had scattered; the main army had already returned; the Emperor led his own two thousand-plus horsemen as rearguard and camped overnight at Cucumber Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians had scattered and the main army was gone; he led two thousand horsemen as rearguard and camped at Cucumber Mound.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕別部數萬騎，扣鞍而進，四面圍逼，帝安睡，平明方起，神色自若，指畫軍形，潰圍而出。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of horsemen of a separate Rouran division advanced with hands on saddles, surrounding on all four sides; the Emperor slept peacefully, rose only at dawn, his expression unchanged, directed the army formation, and broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Rouran horsemen surrounded him; he slept until dawn, rose calm, deployed his men, and broke out.

sentences.zh: 虜走，追擊之，伏尸二十里，獲菴羅辰妻子、生口三萬餘。

translations.literal: The barbarians fled; he pursued them; corpses lay for twenty li; he captured Yanluochen's wife and children and more than thirty thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing barbarians for twenty li of corpses and took Yanluochen's family and thirty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 五月丁亥，地豆干、契丹並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai Didougan and the Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Didougan and the Khitan sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 丁未，北討蠕蠕，又大破之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei he marched north against Rouran and again routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he marched north and again crushed the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 六月，蠕蠕遠遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Rouran fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Rouran fled far away.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，西魏攻陷江陵，殺梁元帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Western Wei captured and took Jiangling, killing Emperor Yuan of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Western Wei took Jiangling and killed Liang's Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 梁將王僧辯在建業，推其晉安王蕭方智為太宰、都督中外諸軍事、承制置百官。

translations.literal: Liang general Wang Sengbian was at Jiankang and installed their Prince of Jin'an Xiao Fangzhi as Grand Mentor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, and Holder of Imperial Authority, establishing the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiankang Liang general Wang Sengbian made Prince of Jin'an Xiao Fangzhi Grand Mentor and Commander-in-Chief with imperial authority and set up the offices.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚申，車駕北巡，至達速嶺，親覽山川險要，將起長城。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen of the twelfth month the imperial carriage toured north to Dasu Ridge, personally surveyed the mountains and rivers and strategic points, and planned to build the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen of the twelfth month he toured north to Dasu Ridge, surveyed the terrain, and planned the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 是歲，西魏恭帝元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Emperor Gong of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Western Wei Emperor Gong year one.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月壬寅，清河王岳度江，剋夏首。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, on the day renyin, Prince of Qinghe Yue crossed the river and took Xia Head.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, first month, on renyin, Prince of Qinghe Yue crossed the river and took Xia Head.

sentences.zh: 梁司徒、郢州刺史陸法和請降。

translations.literal: Liang Minister of Works and Inspector of Ying Province Lu Fahe requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Minister of Works and Inspector of Ying Lu Fahe surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔以梁貞陽侯蕭明為梁主，遣尚書右僕射、上黨王渙送之江南。

translations.literal: An edict made Liang Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming ruler of Liang and sent Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Shangdang Huan, to escort him to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming ruler of Liang and sent Prince of Shangdang Huan to escort him to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 二月甲子，以陸法和為使持節、都督十州諸軍事、太尉、大都督、西南道大行臺。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi of the second month Lu Fahe was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of Military Affairs of Ten Provinces, Grand Commandant, Grand Commander, and Grand Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the second month Lu Fahe became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of Ten Provinces, Grand Commandant, Grand Commander, and Grand Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌，上黨王渙剋東關，斬梁將裴之橫。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu Prince of Shangdang Huan took East Pass and beheaded Liang general Pei Zhiheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince of Shangdang Huan took East Pass and beheaded Liang general Pei Zhiheng.

sentences.zh: 丙申，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 封文襄二子，孝珩為廣寧王，延宗為安德王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Wenxiang's two sons: Xiaohang as Prince of Guangning and Yanzong as Prince of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Wenxiang's sons Xiaohang as Prince of Guangning and Yanzong as Prince of Ande.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝臨昭陽殿決獄。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu the Emperor presided over cases at Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Emperor judged cases at Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 是月，發寡婦以配軍士築長城。

translations.literal: That month widows were conscripted to be paired with soldiers for building the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: That month widows were assigned to soldiers to build the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，蕭明入于建業。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xiao Ming entered Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xiao Ming entered Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子，河東王潘相樂薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiazi, Prince of Hedong Pan Xiangyue died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Prince of Hedong Pan Xiangyue died.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝親討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: On the day renshen the Emperor personally attacked Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Emperor attacked Rouran in person.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，諸軍大會祁連池。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu the armies assembled at Qilian Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the armies gathered at Qilian Pool.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，出塞，至厙狄谷，百餘里無水泉，六軍渴乏，俄而大雨。

translations.literal: On the day yihai they went beyond the frontier to Kudi Valley; for more than a hundred li there were no springs; the six armies were parched with thirst, then suddenly great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai they crossed the frontier to Kudi Valley; for a hundred li there was no water and the army thirsted, then rain fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，帝頓白道，留輜重，親率輕騎五千，追蠕蠕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day jimao, the Emperor halted at White Road, left the baggage train, and personally led five thousand light horsemen in pursuit of Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jimao, he halted at White Road, left the baggage, and led five thousand light horse in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 壬午，及之懷朔鎮。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he caught them at Huaishuo Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he overtook them at Huaishuo Garrison.

sentences.zh: 帝躬犯矢石，頻大破之，遂至沃野。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself braved arrows and stones, repeatedly routed them utterly, and advanced to Woye.
translations.idiomatic: He himself braved arrow and stone, broke them again and again, and reached Woye.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月己卯，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jimao, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jimao, the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗、庫莫奚並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Goguryeo and Kumo Xi both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Goguryeo and Kumo Xi sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔發夫一百八十萬人築長城，自幽州北夏口，西至恒州，九百餘里。

translations.literal: An edict conscripted 1.8 million laborers to build the Long Wall from Beixia Pass north of You Province west to Heng Province, more than nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: An edict conscripted 1.8 million men to build the Long Wall from Beixia Pass in You Province west to Heng Province, over nine hundred li.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月辛丑，封司空侯莫陳相為白水郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day xinchou, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang was enfeoffed as Prince of Baishui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, first month, on xinchou, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang became Prince of Baishui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 於鄴城西馬射，大集衆庶觀之。

translations.literal: West of Ye he held mounted archery, gathering the multitude to watch.
translations.idiomatic: West of Ye he held mounted archery before a great crowd.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未，詔常山王演等於涼風堂讀尚書奏案，論定得失，帝親決之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei of the second month an edict had Prince of Changshan Yan and others read memorials from the Masters of Writing at Cool Wind Hall, discuss right and wrong, and the Emperor decided in person.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei of the second month Prince of Changshan Yan and others debated memorials at Cool Wind Hall while the Emperor decided.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，大都督蕭軌等帥衆濟江。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the third month Grand Commander Xiao Gui and others led troops across the river.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of the third month Grand Commander Xiao Gui crossed the river with troops.

sentences.zh: 六月乙卯，蕭軌等與梁師戰於鍾山西，遇霖雨失利，軌及都督李希光、王敬寶、東方老、軍司裴英起並沒，士卒還者十二三。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yimao, Xiao Gui and others fought Liang forces west of Mount Zhong; they met with heavy rain and were defeated; Gui and Commanders Li Xiguang, Wang Jingbao, Dongfang Lao, and Army Supervisor Pei Yingqi all perished; only one or two in ten soldiers returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao of the sixth month Xiao Gui fought Liang west of Mount Zhong, lost in heavy rain; Gui, Li Xiguang, Wang Jingbao, Dongfang Lao, and Pei Yingqi died; only one or two soldiers in ten returned.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，梁湘州刺史王琳獻馴象。

translations.literal: On the day yichou Wang Lin, Inspector of Xiang Province of Liang, presented a tame elephant.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Liang's Inspector of Xiang Wang Lin presented a tame elephant.

sentences.zh: 秋七月。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，周文帝殂。

translations.literal: On the day yihai Wen of Zhou died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Zhou's Wen died.

sentences.zh: 是月，發山東寡婦二千六百人配軍士，有夫而濫奪者十二三。

translations.literal: That month 2,600 widows of Shandong were assigned to soldiers; one or two in ten had husbands and were wrongly taken.
translations.idiomatic: That month 2,600 Shandong widows were assigned to soldiers; one or two in ten were wrongly taken from husbands.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子，併省州三，郡一百五十三，縣五百八十九，鎮三，戍二十六。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renzi, three provinces, 153 commanderies, 589 counties, 3 garrisons, and 26 outposts were merged and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi of the eleventh month three provinces, 153 commanderies, 589 counties, and 29 posts were consolidated.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚子，魏恭帝遜位於周。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the twelfth month Emperor Gong of Wei abdicated to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi of the twelfth month Wei's Emperor Gong abdicated to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，庫莫奚、契丹遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Kumo Xi and the Khitan sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Kumo Xi and the Khitan sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 脩廣三臺宮殿。

translations.literal: The Three Terraces palace was expanded and broadened.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Terraces palace was enlarged.

sentences.zh: 先是，自西河總秦戍築長城東至海，前後所築，東西凡三千餘里，六十里一戍，其要害置州鎮凡二十五所。

translations.literal: Earlier, from Zongqin Garrison in Xihe the Long Wall was built east to the sea; in all, east and west, more than three thousand li were built, a garrison every sixty li, and at strategic points twenty-five provinces and garrisons were established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Long Wall ran from Zongqin Garrison in Xihe east to the sea, three thousand li in all, a post every sixty li, with twenty-five provincial garrisons at key points.

sentences.zh: 八年春三月，大熱，人或暍死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year, spring, great heat; some died of sunstroke.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, third month, heat was so fierce that some died of sunstroke.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚午，詔禁取蝦蟹蜆蛤之類，唯許私家捕魚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the day gengwu, an edict forbade taking shrimp, crabs, clams, and the like; only private fishing was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu of the fourth month an edict forbade taking shellfish; only private fishing was allowed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔公私禁取鷹鷂。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou an edict forbade public and private taking of hawks and falcons.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an edict forbade taking hawks and falcons.

sentences.zh: 以太師、咸陽王斛律金為右丞相，以前大將軍、扶風王可朱渾道元為太傅，以開府儀同三司賀拔仁為太保，尚書令、常山王演為司空、錄尚書事，以長廣王湛為尚書令，以尚書右僕射楊愔為左僕射，以并省尚書右僕射崔暹為右僕射，以上黨王渙為錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xianyang Hulu Jin was made Right Chancellor; former Grand General, Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Daoyuan was made Grand Tutor; Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies Heba Ren was made Grand Mentor; Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Changshan Yan was made Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Changgang Zhan was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin was made Left Vice Minister; Bing Province Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Xian was made Right Vice Minister; Prince of Shangdang Huan was made Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Jin became Right Chancellor, Kezhuhun Daoyuan Grand Tutor, Heba Ren Grand Mentor, Prince of Changshan Yan Minister of Works and Recorder, Prince of Changgang Zhan Director of the Masters of Writing, Yang Yin Left Vice Minister, Cui Xian Right Vice Minister, and Prince of Shangdang Huan Recorder.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝在城東馬射，敕京師士女悉赴觀，不赴者，罪以軍法，七日乃止。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor held mounted archery east of the city and ordered the men and women of the capital all to attend; those who did not came under military law; it lasted seven days before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: That month he held archery east of the city and ordered all capital men and women to watch; absentees faced military punishment for seven days.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉，冀州人劉向於鄴謀逆，黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinyou, Liu Xiang of Ji Province plotted rebellion at Ye; his associates were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou of the fifth month Liu Xiang of Ji Province rebelled at Ye and his party was executed.

sentences.zh: 秋八月己巳，庫莫奚遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jisi, Kumo Xi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi of the eighth month Kumo Xi sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔丘郊禘祫時祭，皆市取少牢，不得刲割，有司監視，必令豐備；

translations.literal: On the day gengchen an edict ordered that for suburban sacrifices at the mound, seasonal offerings, and di and xia rites, young livestock were to be purchased in the market and not slaughtered on site; officials were to supervise and ensure abundance;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an edict required market purchase of sacrificial animals for state rites, with no on-site slaughter, under official supervision;

sentences.zh: 農社、先蠶，酒肉而已；

translations.literal: for agricultural altars and the First Silkworm, wine and meat only;
translations.idiomatic: agricultural altars and First Silkworm received only wine and meat;

sentences.zh: 雩、禖、風、雨、司人、司祿、靈星雜祀，果餅酒脯。

translations.literal: for rain, marriage, wind, rain, Director of Men, Director of Salary, and Spirit Star miscellaneous rites, fruit, cakes, wine, and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: miscellaneous rites received fruit, cakes, wine, and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 唯當務盡誠敬，義同如在。

translations.literal: Only utmost sincerity and reverence were required, with the meaning of "as if present."
translations.idiomatic: Only sincerity was required, as if the spirits were present.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，制榷酤。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi monopolies on wine were established.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi wine monopolies were established.

sentences.zh: 自夏至九月，河北六州、河南十三州、畿內八郡大蝗，飛至鄴，蔽日，聲如風雨。

translations.literal: From summer solstice through the ninth month, six provinces of Hebei, thirteen of Henan, and eight metropolitan commanderies suffered great locusts; swarms flew to Ye, blotting the sun, their sound like wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through the ninth month locusts ravaged Hebei, Henan, and the capital region; swarms darkened Ye like a storm.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔今年遭蝗處，免租。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen an edict remitted rent in places struck by locusts this year.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen rent was remitted where locusts had struck.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙亥，梁主蕭方智遜位於陳。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the day yihai, Liang ruler Xiao Fangzhi abdicated to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai of the tenth month Liang's Xiao Fangzhi abdicated to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝遣使稱藩朝貢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen sent envoys declaring himself a vassal with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's Emperor Wu sent envoys declaring vassalage and tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周閔帝元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Emperor Min of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Zhou Emperor Min year one.

sentences.zh: 周冢宰宇文護殺閔帝而立明帝，又改元焉。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Zhou Yuwen Hu killed Emperor Min and installed Emperor Ming, again changing the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chancellor Yuwen Hu killed Emperor Min, set up Emperor Ming, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 初於長城內築重城，庫洛拔而東，至於塢紇戍，凡四百餘里。

translations.literal: At first an inner wall was built within the Long Wall from Kuluo east to Wuge Garrison, in all more than four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: First an inner wall was built within the Long Wall from Kuluo east to Wuge Garrison, over four hundred li.

sentences.zh: 九年春二月丁亥，降罪人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, on the day dinghai, criminals were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, second month, on dinghai criminals were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔燎野限以仲冬，不得他時行火，損昆蟲草木。

translations.literal: On the day jichou an edict limited burning the fields to mid-winter; fire at other times harmed insects and plants.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou an edict limited field-burning to mid-winter to spare insects and plants.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the third month the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of the third month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the day xinsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the fourth month the realm was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 是月，北豫州刺史司馬消難以城叛于周。

translations.literal: That month Inspector of Beiyu Province Sima Xiaonan rebelled with his city to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Beiyu Inspector Sima Xiaonan surrendered his city to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 大旱，帝以祈雨不降，毀西門豹祠，掘其冢。

translations.literal: Great drought; because prayers for rain failed, the Emperor destroyed the shrine of Ximen Bao and dug up his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In great drought, when rain prayers failed, he destroyed Ximen Bao's shrine and dug up his tomb.

sentences.zh: 五月辛丑，以尚書令、長廣王湛為錄尚書事，以驃騎大將軍、平秦王歸彥為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinchou, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Changgang Zhan was made Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and General of Fast Cavalry, Prince of Pingqin Guiyan was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou of the fifth month Prince of Changgang Zhan became Recorder and Prince of Pingqin Guiyan Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以前左僕射楊愔為尚書令。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen former Left Vice Minister Yang Yin was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen former Left Vice Minister Yang Yin became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，帝自晉陽北巡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yichou, the Emperor toured north from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou of the sixth month he toured north from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 己巳，至祁連池。

translations.literal: On the day jisi he reached Qilian Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he reached Qilian Pool.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是夏，山東大蝗，差人夫捕而坑之。

translations.literal: That summer Shandong suffered great locusts; laborers were sent to catch and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Shandong swarmed with locusts; laborers were sent to catch and bury them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛丑，給畿內老人劉奴等九百四十三人版職及杖帽，各有差。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day xinchou, 943 elderly men of the capital region including Liu Nu were given official rank, staffs, and caps, each according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou of the seventh month 943 elderly men including Liu Nu received rank, staffs, and caps by degree.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔趙、燕、瀛、定、南營五州，及司州廣平、清河二郡，去年螽澇損田，兼春夏少雨，苗稼薄者，免今年租稅。

translations.literal: On the day wushen an edict remitted this year's rent and tax in Zhao, Yan, Ying, Ding, and Southern Camp five provinces and Guangping and Qinghe two commanderies of Si Province, where locusts and floods had damaged fields last year and spring and summer rains had been scant.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen rent was remitted in five provinces and two commanderies where locusts, flood, and drought had ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day yichou, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou of the eighth month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu he traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，發丁匠三十餘萬人營三臺於鄴，因其舊基而高博之，大起宮室及遊豫園。
