translations.literal: Earlier more than 300,000 craftsmen and laborers had been conscripted to build the Three Terraces at Ye, raising the old foundations higher and broader, and greatly erecting palaces and pleasure gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier 300,000 craftsmen had been conscripted to raise the Three Terraces at Ye and build palaces and pleasure gardens.

sentences.zh: 至是，三臺成。

translations.literal: By this time the Three Terraces were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Three Terraces were finished.

sentences.zh: 改銅爵曰金鳳，金武曰聖應，冰井曰崇光。

translations.literal: Bronze Sparrow was renamed Golden Phoenix, Golden Martial became Sacred Response, and Ice Well became Chongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze Sparrow became Golden Phoenix, Golden Martial Sacred Response, Ice Well Chongguang.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月甲午，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiawu, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu of the eleventh month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 登三臺，御乾象殿，朝宴羣臣。

translations.literal: He ascended the Three Terraces, took his seat in the Qianxiang Hall, and held court feast for the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the Three Terraces, sat in Qianxiang Hall, and feasted his ministers.

sentences.zh: 以新宮成，丁酉，大赦內外，文武官並進一大階。

translations.literal: Because the new palace was complete, on the day dingyou a general amnesty was proclaimed within and without, and civil and military officials were each advanced one full rank.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, with the new palace complete, he pardoned the realm and raised all officials one rank.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，梁湘州刺史王琳遣使請立蕭莊為梁主，仍以江州內屬，令莊居之。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi Wang Lin, Inspector of Xiang Province of Liang, sent envoys requesting that Xiao Zhuang be installed as ruler of Liang, with Jiang Province submitting and Zhuang residing there.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Liang's Wang Lin asked that Xiao Zhuang be made ruler of Liang with Jiang Province submitting.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，詔以梁王蕭莊為梁主，進居九派。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou an edict made Prince of Liang Xiao Zhuang ruler of Liang and advanced him to Jiupai.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou an edict made Prince of Liang Xiao Zhuang ruler of Liang at Jiupai.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，太傅以可朱渾道元為太師，以司徒尉粲為太尉，以冀州刺史段韶為司空，以錄尚書事、常山王演為大司馬，以錄尚書事、長廣王湛為司徒。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin Grand Tutor Kezhuhun Daoyuan was made Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works Wei Can was made Grand Commandant, Inspector of Ji Province Duan Shao was made Minister of Works, Recorder of Affairs Prince of Changshan Yan was made Grand Marshal, and Recorder Prince of Changgang Zhan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Kezhuhun Daoyuan became Grand Preceptor, Wei Can Grand Commandant, Duan Shao Minister of Works, Prince of Changshan Yan Grand Marshal, and Prince of Changgang Zhan Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 起大莊嚴寺。

translations.literal: The Great Zhuangyan Monastery was begun.
translations.idiomatic: Work began on the Great Zhuangyan Monastery.

sentences.zh: 是歲，殺永安王浚、上黨王渙。

translations.literal: That year Prince of Yong'an Jun and Prince of Shangdang Huan were killed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Princes Yong'an Jun and Shangdang Huan were killed.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月戊戌，以司空侯莫陳相為大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, on the day wuxu, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, first month, on wuxu, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang became Grand General.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太尉長樂郡公尉粲、肆州刺史濮陽公婁仲遠並進爵為王。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou Grand Commandant Duke of Changle Commandery Wei Can and Inspector of Si Province Duke of Puyang Commandery Lou Zhongyuan were both advanced in noble rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Grand Commandant Wei Can and Si Inspector Lou Zhongyuan were both raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，行幸遼陽甘露寺。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin he traveled to Ganlu Monastery in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he visited Ganlu Monastery in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，帝於甘露寺禪居深觀，唯軍國大政奏聞。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu of the second month the Emperor dwelt in Chan retreat at Ganlu Monastery in deep contemplation; only great matters of state and army were reported.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu of the second month he withdrew to Chan at Ganlu Monastery; only great state and military affairs were reported.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，以侍中高德正為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of the third month Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu of the third month Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng became Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，車駕至自遼陽。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen the imperial carriage returned from Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the emperor returned from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，梁主蕭莊至郢州，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month Liang ruler Xiao Zhuang reached Ying Province and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liang's Xiao Zhuang reached Ying Province and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏閏四月丁酉，以司州牧、彭城王浟為兼司空，以侍中、高陽王湜為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, on the day dingyou, Governor of Si Province Prince of Pengcheng You was made Concurrent Minister of Works, and Palace Attendant Prince of Gaoyang Shi was made Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month, on dingyou, Prince of Pengcheng You became Concurrent Minister of Works and Prince of Gaoyang Shi Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以兼司空、彭城王浟為兼太尉，攝司空事，封皇子紹廉為長樂王。

translations.literal: On the day yisi Concurrent Minister of Works Prince of Pengcheng You was made Concurrent Grand Commandant, acting Minister of Works affairs, and the imperial son Shaolian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Prince of Pengcheng You became Concurrent Grand Commandant acting Minister of Works, and Prince Shaolian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 五月癸未，誅始平公元世、東平公元景式等二十五家，禁止特進元韶等十九家。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei twenty-five clans including Prince of Shiping Yuan Shi and Prince of Dongping Yuan Jingshi were executed, and nineteen clans including Special Court Advisor Yuan Shao were placed under prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei twenty-five Yuan clans including Princes Shiping and Dongping were executed and nineteen clans including Yuan Shao were confined.

sentences.zh: 尋並誅之，男子無少長皆斬，所殺三千人，並投漳水。

translations.literal: Soon they were all executed as well; males of every age were beheaded; 3,000 were killed and all cast into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were killed; every male was beheaded; 3,000 bodies were thrown into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 六月，陳武帝殂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Emperor Wu of Chen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chen's Emperor Wu died.

sentences.zh: 秋八月戊戌，封皇子紹義為廣陽王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuxu, the imperial son Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu of the eighth month Prince Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射、河間王孝琬為左僕射。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Hejian Xiaowan was made Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian Xiaowan became Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔諸軍人，或有父祖改姓冒入元氏，或假託攜認，妄稱姓元者，不問世數遠近，悉聽改復本姓。

translations.literal: On the day guimao an edict ordered that soldiers whose fathers or grandfathers had changed surnames to infiltrate the Yuan clan, or who falsely claimed Yuan descent, regardless how many generations distant, were all permitted to restore their original surnames.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao an edict let soldiers who had falsely taken the Yuan surname restore their original names.

sentences.zh: 是月，殺左僕射高德正。

translations.literal: That month Left Vice Minister Gao Dezheng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That month Left Vice Minister Gao Dezheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 九月己巳，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jisi, he traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi of the ninth month he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝沈敏有遠量，外若不遠，內鑒甚明。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deep, keen, and far-sighted; outwardly he seemed not to reach far, yet inwardly his perception was very clear.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep and far-sighted; outwardly dull, inwardly piercingly clear.

sentences.zh: 文襄年長英秀，神武特所愛重，百僚承風，莫不震懼。

translations.literal: Wenxiang was elder, talented, and splendid; Shenwu especially loved and valued him; the hundred officials followed the wind and none failed to tremble in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang was elder, brilliant, and Shenwu's favorite; officials quaked before him.

sentences.zh: 而帝善自晦迹，言不出口，恒自貶退，言咸順從，故深見輕，雖家人亦以為不及。

translations.literal: But the Emperor was skilled at hiding his tracks; words did not leave his mouth; he always belittled himself and spoke in full compliance, and so was deeply underestimated—even his family thought him inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Emperor hid his light; he seldom spoke, always deferred, and even his family thought him lesser.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣業，帝以次長見猜嫌，帝后李氏色美，每預宴會，容貌遠過靖德皇后，文襄彌不平焉。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the enterprise, the Emperor as next eldest was viewed with suspicion; the Empress Lady Li was beautiful and often attended banquets, her looks far surpassing Empress Jingde; Wenxiang was ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang succeeded, the younger Emperor aroused suspicion; Empress Li, surpassing Empress Jingde in beauty at banquets, displeased Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝每為后私營服翫，小佳，文襄即令逼取。

translations.literal: The Emperor often privately obtained finery for the Empress; when it was even slightly fine, Wenxiang at once ordered it seized.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor secretly obtained finery for the Empress; Wenxiang seized whatever pleased him.

sentences.zh: 后恚，有時未與。

translations.literal: The Empress was angry and sometimes would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress sometimes refused.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「此物猶應可求，兄須，何容吝。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "This thing ought still to be obtainable; if brother wants it, how can one be stingy?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed, "Brother wants it? How can I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」文襄或愧而不取，便恭受，亦無飾讓。

translations.literal: Wenxiang would sometimes be ashamed and not take it, yet accept with respect and make no show of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes Wenxiang was ashamed and declined; sometimes he took it without pretense.

sentences.zh: 每退朝還第，輒閉閤靜坐，雖對妻子，能竟日不言。

translations.literal: Each time he returned from court to his residence he would shut the doors and sit in silence; even before wife and children he could go a whole day without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from court he shut his doors and sat silent all day, even before wife and children.

sentences.zh: 或袒跣奔躍，后問其故，對曰：「為爾漫戲。

translations.literal: Sometimes he ran barefoot in frenzy; the Empress asked the reason, and he answered, "Just playing with you."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he ran barefoot; asked why, he said, "Just playing with you."

sentences.zh: 」此蓋習勞而不肯言也。

translations.literal: This was habit laboring in him and his unwillingness to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: This was discipline he would not speak of.

sentences.zh: 所寢至夜曾有光，巨細可察，后驚告帝，帝曰：「慎勿妄言。

translations.literal: The place where he slept at night sometimes had light by which the smallest detail could be seen; the Empress was startled and told the Emperor, who said, "Be careful not to speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: His bedchamber sometimes shone at night; the Empress was alarmed; he said, "Tell no one."

sentences.zh: 」自此唯與后寢，侍御皆令出外。

translations.literal: From this time he slept only with the Empress and ordered all attendants to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he slept only with the Empress and dismissed all attendants.

sentences.zh: 文襄崩，祕不發喪，其後漸露，魏帝竊謂左右曰：「大將軍此殂，似是天意，威權當歸王室矣。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang died the death was kept secret, then gradually leaked; the Wei Emperor whispered to those beside him, "The Grand General's death seems heaven's will; authority should return to the imperial house."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang died the secret leaked; the Wei Emperor whispered, "Heaven has taken the Grand General; power should return to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」及帝將赴晉陽，親入辭謁於昭陽殿，從者千人，居前持劒者十餘輩。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was to go to Jinyang he entered in person to take leave at Zhaoyang Hall with a thousand followers; more than ten men ahead bore swords.
translations.idiomatic: Going to Jinyang, he took leave at Zhaoyang Hall with a thousand followers, a dozen swordsmen ahead.

sentences.zh: 帝在殿下數十步立，而衞士升階已二百許人，皆攘袂扣刃，若對嚴敵。

translations.literal: The Emperor stood several tens of paces below the hall while already two hundred-odd guards had ascended the steps, sleeves rolled and blades drawn as if facing stern foes.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall he stood while two hundred guards on the steps bared blades as for battle.

sentences.zh: 帝令主者傳奏，須詣晉陽，言訖，再拜而出。

translations.literal: The Emperor had the usher announce that he must go to Jinyang; when he had spoken he bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He announced his departure for Jinyang, bowed twice, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏帝失色，目送帝曰：「此人似不能見容，吾不知死在何日。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor turned pale and watched him go, saying, "This man seems unable to bear me; I do not know on what day I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor paled and said, "This man will not spare me; I know not the day of my death."

sentences.zh: 」及至并州，慰諭將士，措辭款實。

translations.literal: When he reached Bing Province he comforted the soldiers; his words were sincere and solid.
translations.idiomatic: At Bing Province he comforted the troops in plain, honest words.

sentences.zh: 衆皆欣然，曰：「誰謂左僕射翻不減令公。

translations.literal: All were pleased and said, "Who says Left Vice Minister Fan does not match the Duke?"
translations.idiomatic: All rejoiced: "Who says Vice Minister Fan falls short of the Duke?"

sentences.zh: 」令公即指文襄也。

translations.literal: "The Duke" meant Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: "The Duke" meant Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 時訛言上黨出聖人，帝聞之，將徙一郡。

translations.literal: At the time a false report said a sage had appeared in Shangdang; when the Emperor heard it, he was about to move an entire commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor said a sage had risen in Shangdang; the Emperor nearly moved a whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 而郡人張思進上言，殿下生於南宮，坊名上黨，即是上黨出聖人，帝悅而止。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Zhang Sijin, memorialized: "Your Highness was born in the Southern Palace; the ward is named Shangdang—this is the sage from Shangdang." The Emperor was pleased and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sijin said, "You were born in the Southern Palace ward called Shangdang—that is the sage." The Emperor was pleased and desisted.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「一束藁，兩頭然，河邊羖437d飛上天。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said, "A bundle of straw, both ends burning; a ram by the river flies up to heaven."
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme ran: "A bundle of straw burns at both ends; a ram by the river flies to heaven."

sentences.zh: 」藁然兩頭，於文為高；

translations.literal: Straw burning at both ends—in writing this forms the character for Gao;
translations.idiomatic: Burning at both ends forms the character for Gao;

sentences.zh: 河邊羖437d為水邊羊，指帝名也。

translations.literal: a ram by the river is a sheep by water, pointing to the Emperor's name.
translations.idiomatic: a ram by the river is a sheep by water, the Emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 於是徐之才盛陳宜受禪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xu Zhicai strongly urged that he should receive the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicai then urged acceptance of the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「先父亡兄，功德如此，尚終北面，吾又何敢當。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "My late father and elder brother achieved such merit yet remained facing north; how dare I accept?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Father and brother achieved such merit yet served another; how dare I?"

sentences.zh: 」之才曰：「正為不及父兄，須早升九五，如其不作，人將生心。

translations.literal: Zhicai said, "Precisely because you fall short of father and brother you must ascend early; if you do not, men will turn their hearts. And the prophecy says, 'A ram drinks at Meng Ford, horns propping heaven.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "Because you fall short of them you must rise early, or hearts will turn."

sentences.zh: 且讖云『羊飲盟津角拄天』，盟津水也，羊飲水，王名也，角拄天，大位也。

translations.literal: "Meng Ford is water; a ram drinking water is the king's name; horns propping heaven is the great position."
translations.idiomatic: "Meng Ford is water; a ram drinking water is the king's name; horns to heaven is the throne."

sentences.zh: 又陽平郡界面星驛傍有大水，土人常見羣羊數百，立卧其中，就視不見，事與讖合，願王勿疑。

translations.literal: Also at Jie Star Post in Yangping Commandery beside a great water, locals often saw hundreds of sheep standing and lying in it; when approached they vanished; the matter matched the prophecy; he begged the prince not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: At Jie Star Post locals saw hundreds of sheep in the water that vanished when approached; the prophecy matched; he begged the prince not to doubt.

sentences.zh: 」帝以問高德正，德正又贊成之，於是始決。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Gao Dezheng; Dezheng again urged it; thereupon he decided.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Gao Dezheng, who agreed; then he decided.

sentences.zh: 乃使李密卜之，遇大橫，曰：「大吉，漢文帝之卦也。

translations.literal: He had Li Mi divine; he obtained Great Horizontal and said, "Great fortune—the hexagram of Emperor Wen of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi divined Great Horizontal: "Great fortune—the hexagram of Han Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃鑄象以卜之，一寫而成。

translations.literal: The Emperor then cast an image to divine; it was formed in one pouring.
translations.idiomatic: He cast an image to divine; it formed at once.

sentences.zh: 使段韶問斛律金於肆州，金來朝，深言不可，以鎧曹宋景業首陳符命，請殺之。

translations.literal: He sent Duan Shao to ask Hulu Jin at Si Province; Jin came to court and spoke strongly against it; because Armor Bureau Song Jingye first presented the mandate, he requested Jin be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao asked Hulu Jin at Si Province; Jin opposed it; Song Jingye urged killing him.

sentences.zh: 乃議於太后前。

translations.literal: They deliberated before the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They deliberated before the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后謂諸貴曰：「我兒獰直，必自無此意，直高德正樂禍，教之耳。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager told the nobles, "My son is blunt and straight; he surely has no such intent of his own—it is only Gao Dezheng who delights in disaster and teaches him."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "My son is blunt; he has no such intent—only Gao Dezheng teaches him mischief."

sentences.zh: 」帝意決，乃整兵而東。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was set; he then arrayed troops and marched east.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was set; he arrayed troops and marched east.

sentences.zh: 使高德正之鄴，諷喻公卿，莫有應者。

translations.literal: He sent Gao Dezheng to Ye to persuade the ministers; none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng went to Ye to persuade ministers; none responded.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如逆帝於遼陽，固言未可。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru met the Emperor at Liaoyang and firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru met him at Liaoyang and said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 杜弼亦抱馬諫，帝欲還，尚食丞李集曰：「此行事非小，而言還？

translations.literal: Du Bi also embraced the horse and remonstrated; the Emperor wished to return; Palace Provisioner Li Ji said, "This affair is no small matter—yet you speak of returning?"
translations.idiomatic: Du Bi held the horse and remonstrated; the Emperor wished to turn back; Li Ji said, "This is no small matter—return?"

sentences.zh: 」帝偽言使向東門殺之，而別令賜絹十疋。

translations.literal: The Emperor falsely said he was sending him to the eastern gate to be killed, but separately ordered ten bolts of silk given.
translations.idiomatic: He pretended to send Li Ji to the eastern gate for execution, then gave him ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四月，夜，禾生於魏帝銅研，旦長數寸，有穗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, at night, grain grew on the Wei Emperor's bronze inkstone; by dawn it was several inches with ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month grain sprouted on the Wei Emperor's inkstone, several inches with ears by dawn.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝復東赴鄴，令左右曰：「異言者斬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor again went east to Ye and told those beside him, "Whoever speaks otherwise—behead him."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he went east to Ye and said, "Contrary speech means death."

sentences.zh: 」是月，光州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: That month Guang Province presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: That month Guang Province sent a nine-tailed fox.

sentences.zh: 帝至鄴城南，召入，并齎板策。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached the south of Ye, summoned them in, and together brought the tablets and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: South of Ye he summoned them in with tablets and edicts.

sentences.zh: 旦，高隆之進謁曰：「用此何為？

translations.literal: At dawn Gao Longzhi came to audience and said, "What is this for?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Gao Longzhi asked, "What is this for?"

sentences.zh: 」帝作色曰：「我自作事，若欲族滅耶！

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said, "I act on my own—do you wish your clan exterminated?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flushed and said, "I act alone—wish your clan destroyed?"

sentences.zh: 」隆之謝而退。

translations.literal: Longzhi apologized and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi apologized and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是乃作圓丘，備法物，草禪讓事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built the Round Mound, prepared ritual objects, and drafted abdication affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Round Mound, prepared ritual objects, and drafted abdication rites.

sentences.zh: 及登極之後，神明轉茂，外柔內剛，果於斷割，人莫能窺。

translations.literal: After ascending the throne his spirit grew ever more abundant; outwardly gentle, inwardly firm, decisive in cutting and judging—none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement his spirit flourished; outwardly soft, inwardly hard, decisive beyond reading.

sentences.zh: 又特明吏事，留心政術，簡靖寬和，坦於任使，故楊愔等得盡於匡贊，朝政粲然。

translations.literal: He was especially clear in official affairs, attentive to government, simple, quiet, broad, and easy in employment, so Yang Yin and others could fully assist; court governance was brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered official business, favored simple rule, and let Yang Yin and others govern brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 兼以法馭下，不避權貴，或有違犯，不容勳戚，內外莫不肅然。

translations.literal: He also governed subordinates by law, not avoiding the powerful; when there were violations he spared neither kin nor merit; within and without all were awed.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled by law without sparing kin or merit; all were awed.

sentences.zh: 至於軍國機策，獨決懷抱，規謀宏遠，有人君大略。

translations.literal: As for military and state strategy he decided alone in his breast; his plans were vast and he had the great outline of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: On military and state affairs he decided alone with a ruler's grand vision.

sentences.zh: 又以三方鼎峙，繕甲練兵，左右宿衞，置百保軍士。

translations.literal: Because the three realms stood in rivalry he repaired armor and trained troops; for guards left and right he established the Hundred Guards army.
translations.idiomatic: With three realms contending he trained troops and established the Hundred Guards.

sentences.zh: 每臨行陣，親當矢石，鋒刃交接，唯恐前敵不多。

translations.literal: Each time he went to battle he personally faced arrows and stones; when blades crossed he feared only that the enemy ahead were too few.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he faced arrows and stones himself and wished only for more enemies ahead.

sentences.zh: 屢犯艱厄，常致剋捷。

translations.literal: Repeatedly encountering hardship he often achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Through hardship he often won.

sentences.zh: 嘗追及蠕蠕，令都督高阿那肱率騎數千，塞其走道。

translations.literal: Once pursuing Rouran he ordered Commander Gao Anaguzhi to lead several thousand horse and block their escape route.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Rouran he sent Gao Anaguzhi with thousands of horse to block their escape.

sentences.zh: 時虜軍猶盛，五萬餘人。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian army was still strong—more than fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians still numbered fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 肱以兵少請益，帝更減其半騎。

translations.literal: Anaguzhi because his troops were few requested reinforcements; the Emperor further halved his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Anaguzhi asked for more troops; the Emperor halved his cavalry.

sentences.zh: 那肱奮擊，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Anaguzhi struck fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Anaguzhi charged and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 虜主踰越巖谷，僅以身免。

translations.literal: The barbarian khan crossed mountain valleys and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The khan fled over the mountains barely alive.

sentences.zh: 都督高元海、王師羅並無武藝，先稱怯弱，一旦交鋒，有踰驍壯。

translations.literal: Commanders Gao Yuanhai and Wang Siluo had no martial skill and were first called timid; once blades crossed they surpassed the brave.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Gao Yuanhai and Wang Siluo, called timid, fought like the brave when blades met.

sentences.zh: 嘗於東山游宴，以關隴未平，投盃震怒，召魏收於前，立為詔書，宣示遠近，將事西行。

translations.literal: Once feasting on the eastern hills, because Guanlong was not yet pacified he threw his cup in rage, summoned Wei Shou before him, had him draft an edict on the spot to proclaim far and near, and planned a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting on the eastern hills, angry that Guanlong was not pacified, he summoned Wei Shou and proclaimed a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周文帝殂，西人震恐，常為度隴之計。

translations.literal: That year Wen of Zhou died; men of the west were shaken with fear and often planned to cross Long.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhou's Wen died; the west was shaken and planned to cross Long.

sentences.zh: 旣征伐四剋，威振戎夏，六七年後，以功業自矜，遂留情耽湎，肆行淫暴。

translations.literal: Having conquered on four sides and awed the barbarians and Chinese, six or seven years later he took pride in his achievement, then gave himself to drink and debauchery and practiced wanton cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: After six or seven years of conquest he grew proud, then turned to drink, debauchery, and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 或躬自鼓舞，歌謳不息，從旦通宵，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: Sometimes he danced himself, singing without cease from dawn through the night, day following day.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he danced and sang from dawn through the night without cease.

sentences.zh: 或袒露形體，塗傅粉黛，散髮胡服，雜衣錦綵，拔刃張弓，游行巿肆。

translations.literal: Sometimes he exposed his body, smeared powder and rouge, wore loose hair and barbarian dress, mixed silks, drew blade and bent bow, and roamed the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he painted his face, wore barbarian dress, drew bow and blade, and roamed the markets.

sentences.zh: 勳戚之第，朝夕臨幸。

translations.literal: He visited the mansions of kin and merit morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He visited kin and merit morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 時乘鹿車、白象、駱駞、牛、驢，並不施鞍勒。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode deer carts, white elephants, camels, oxen, and donkeys without saddle or bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He rode deer carts, elephants, camels, oxen, and donkeys without saddles.

sentences.zh: 或盛暑炎赫，日中暴身，隆冬酷寒，去衣馳走，從者不堪，帝居之自若。

translations.literal: In fierce summer heat he exposed himself at noon; in bitter winter cold he ran naked—followers could not bear it yet he was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In summer heat he bared himself at noon; in winter he ran naked while followers suffered.

sentences.zh: 街坐巷宿，處處游行。

translations.literal: He sat in streets and slept in lanes, roaming everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in streets and slept in lanes.

sentences.zh: 多使劉桃枝、崔季舒負之而行。

translations.literal: He often had Liu Taozhi and Cui Jishu carry him on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taozhi and Cui Jishu often carried him.

sentences.zh: 或擔胡鼓而拍之。

translations.literal: Or he beat a barbarian drum.
translations.idiomatic: Or he beat a barbarian drum.

sentences.zh: 親戚貴臣，左右近習，侍從錯雜，無復差等。

translations.literal: Kin, nobles, and attendants were mixed without order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Kin, nobles, and attendants mingled without rank.

sentences.zh: 徵集淫嫗，悉去衣裳，分付從官，朝夕臨視。

translations.literal: He gathered licentious women, stripped them bare, assigned them to attendants, and watched morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped licentious women and had attendants watch them day and night.

sentences.zh: 或聚棘為馬，紐草為索，逼遣乘騎，牽引來去，流血灑地，以為娛樂。

translations.literal: Or he made a horse of thorns and a rope of grass, forced them to ride while others pulled them back and forth until blood soaked the ground for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He made thorn horses and grass ropes, forced women to ride until blood soaked the ground for sport.

sentences.zh: 凡諸殺害，多令支解，或焚之於火，或投之於河。

translations.literal: Of killings in general, many were dismembered, burned in fire, or cast into rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Killings were often by dismemberment, fire, or drowning.

sentences.zh: 沈酗旣久，彌以狂惑，每至將醉，輒拔劒挂手，或張弓傅矢，或執持牟槊。

translations.literal: The longer he drowned in drink the more mad he grew; whenever he was about to be drunk he hung a sword on his hand, or strung a bow with arrows, or held a spear.
translations.idiomatic: Drunken, he hung swords on his hand, strung bows, or held spears.

sentences.zh: 游行巿廛，問婦人曰：「天子何如？

translations.literal: Roaming the markets he asked women, "What is the Son of Heaven like?"
translations.idiomatic: In the markets he asked women, "What is the Son of Heaven like?"

sentences.zh: 」荅曰：「顛顛癡癡，何成天子。

translations.literal: They answered, "Mad and foolish—how could he be Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Mad and foolish—how is that a Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He killed them.

sentences.zh: 或馳騁衢路，散擲錢物，恣人拾取，爭競諠譁，方以為喜。

translations.literal: Or he galloped through crossroads scattering money for people to scramble for, taking the clamor as joy.
translations.idiomatic: He scattered money in crossroads and delighted in the scramble.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗在北宮，坐一小榻，帝時已醉，手自舉牀，后便墜落，頗有傷損。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was once at the Northern Palace on a small couch; the Emperor was drunk and lifted the bed himself; the Empress fell and was somewhat injured.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he lifted the Empress Dowager's couch; she fell and was hurt.

sentences.zh: 醒悟之後，大懷慙恨，遂令多聚柴火，將入其中。

translations.literal: When he sobered he was deeply ashamed and ordered much firewood gathered to enter the fire himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sober, he was ashamed and ordered firewood to burn himself.

sentences.zh: 太后驚懼，親自持挽。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was terrified and held him back herself.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager held him back.

sentences.zh: 又設地席，令平秦王高歸彥執杖，口自責疏，脫背就罰。

translations.literal: He spread a mat on the ground and had Prince of Pingqin Guiyan hold the staff while he himself recited his faults and bared his back for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He had Prince of Pingqin Guiyan beat his bared back while he recited his faults.

sentences.zh: 敕歸彥：「杖不出血，當即斬汝。

translations.literal: He ordered Guiyan, "If the staff draws no blood you are beheaded at once."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guiyan, "No blood means death."

sentences.zh: 」太后涕泣，前自抱之，帝流涕苦請，不肯受於太后。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept and embraced him; the Emperor wept and begged, refusing to accept from the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wept and embraced him; he wept and begged.

sentences.zh: 太后聽許，方捨背杖，笞腳五十，莫不至到。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager consented he stopped the back beating and flogged his feet fifty times—none failed to land.
translations.idiomatic: She consented; he took fifty strokes on the feet.

sentences.zh: 衣冠拜謝，悲不自勝，因此戒酒。

translations.literal: In court dress he bowed in thanks, unable to bear his grief, and thereby stopped drinking.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed in thanks and stopped drinking.

sentences.zh: 一旬，還復如初。

translations.literal: After ten days he returned to as before.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days he drank as before.

sentences.zh: 自是耽湎轉劇。

translations.literal: From this his debauchery grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Debauchery grew worse.

sentences.zh: 遂幸李后家，以鳴鏑射后母崔，正中其頰，因罵曰：「吾醉時尚不識太后，老婢何事！

translations.literal: He then visited Empress Li's home, shot Empress Li's mother Cui with a whistling arrow square in the cheek, and cursed, "When drunk I do not even know the Empress Dowager—what business is it of an old hag!"
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Li's home he shot her mother Cui in the cheek and cursed the old woman.

sentences.zh: 」馬鞭亂打一百有餘。

translations.literal: He whipped her more than a hundred times with a horsewhip.
translations.idiomatic: He horsewhipped her more than a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 三臺構木高二十七丈，兩棟相距二百餘尺，工匠危怯，皆繫繩自防；

translations.literal: The Three Terraces timber structure was twenty-seven zhang high; the two peaks were more than two hundred chi apart; craftsmen in peril tied ropes for protection;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Terraces rose twenty-seven zhang; craftsmen tied ropes in fear;

sentences.zh: 帝登脊疾走，都無怖畏。

translations.literal: the Emperor ran along the ridge without fear.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor ran the ridge without fear.

sentences.zh: 時復雅舞，折旋中節，傍人見者，莫不寒心。

translations.literal: Sometimes he performed elegant dance, turning in perfect time; those who saw it were chilled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: He danced with perfect grace; onlookers shuddered.

sentences.zh: 又召死囚，以席為翅，從臺飛下，免其罪戮。

translations.literal: He also summoned condemned men, made wings of mats, and had them fly from the terrace to pardon their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He had condemned men fly from the terrace on mat wings to win pardon.

sentences.zh: 果敢不慮者，盡皆獲全；

translations.literal: The bold and unhesitating all survived whole;
translations.idiomatic: The bold survived;

sentences.zh: 疑怯猶豫者，或致損跌。

translations.literal: the doubtful and timid sometimes fell and were injured.
translations.idiomatic: the timid sometimes fell injured.

sentences.zh: 沈酗旣久，轉虧本性。

translations.literal: The longer he drowned in drink the more his nature was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Drink further destroyed his nature.

sentences.zh: 怒大司農穆子容，使之脫衣而伏，親射之，不中，以橛貫其下竅，入腸。

translations.literal: Angry at Grand Minister of Agriculture Mu Zirong, he made him strip and lie prone, shot at him personally, missed, and drove a stake through his lower opening into the bowels.
translations.idiomatic: He shot at Mu Zirong, missed, and drove a stake through his body.

sentences.zh: 雖以楊愔為宰輔，使進廁籌。

translations.literal: Though Yang Yin was Chancellor he made him present toilet sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yang Yin was Chancellor he made him present toilet sticks.

sentences.zh: 以其體肥，呼為楊大肚，馬鞭鞭其背，流血浹袍。

translations.literal: Because he was fat he called him Big Belly Yang and horsewhipped his back until blood soaked his robe.
translations.idiomatic: He called fat Yang Yin Big Belly and whipped him until blood soaked his robe.

sentences.zh: 以刀子剺其腹，崔季舒託俳言曰：「老小公子惡戲？

translations.literal: He cut his belly with a knife; Cui Jishu through comic speech said, "Does the young master play rough?"
translations.idiomatic: He cut Yang Yin's belly; Cui Jishu jested, "Does the young master play rough?"

sentences.zh: 」因掣刀子而去之。

translations.literal: and pulled the knife away.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he jerked the knife away.

sentences.zh: 又置愔於棺中，載以轜車，幾下釘者數四。

translations.literal: He also placed Yin in a coffin, carried him in a pall carriage, and nearly drove in nails several times.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yin in a coffin and nearly nailed it shut several times.

sentences.zh: 曾至彭城王浟宅，謂其母尒朱曰：「憶汝辱我母壻時，向何由可耐。

translations.literal: Once at Prince of Pengcheng You's house he said to his mother Erzhu, "Do you remember when you shamed my mother-in-law—how could that be borne?"
translations.idiomatic: At You's house he reminded Erzhu of shaming his mother-in-law and killed her himself.

sentences.zh: 」手自刃殺。

translations.literal: He personally bladed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: He killed her with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 又至故僕射崔暹第，謂暹妻李曰：「頗憶暹不？

translations.literal: He also went to former Vice Minister Cui Xian's house and said to Xian's wife Li, "Do you miss Xian?"
translations.idiomatic: At Cui Xian's house he asked Li, "Do you miss Xian?"

sentences.zh: 」李曰：「結髮義深，實懷追憶。

translations.literal: Li said, "Our hair-bound bond was deep; I truly remember him."
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "Our bond was deep; I remember him."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「若憶時，自往看也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If you miss him, go see him yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Then go see him."

sentences.zh: 」親自斬之，棄頭牆外。

translations.literal: He personally beheaded her and cast the head outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded her and threw the head over the wall.

sentences.zh: 嘗在晉陽，以矟戲刺都督尉子耀，應手而死。

translations.literal: Once at Jinyang he playfully speared Commander Wei Ziyao and killed him at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he speared Commander Wei Ziyao and killed him.

sentences.zh: 在三臺太光殿上，鋸殺都督穆嵩。

translations.literal: On the Great Light Hall of the Three Terraces he sawed Commander Mu Song to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the Great Light Hall he sawed Commander Mu Song to death.

sentences.zh: 又幸開府暴顯家，有都督韓哲無罪，忽衆中召，斬之數段。

translations.literal: He also visited Defender Bao Xian's house; Commander Han Zhe was innocent yet was summoned from the crowd and hacked into several pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At Bao Xian's house he hacked innocent Commander Han Zhe to pieces.

sentences.zh: 魏樂安王元昂，后之姊壻，其妻有色，帝數幸之，欲納為昭儀。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Le'an Yuan Ang, the Empress's sister's husband, had a beautiful wife whom the Emperor often visited and wished to make Lady of Bright Appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince of Le'an Yuan Ang had a beautiful wife whom the Emperor often visited and wished to take.

sentences.zh: 召昂令伏，以鳴鏑射一百餘下，凝血垂將一石，竟至於死。

translations.literal: He summoned Ang and ordered him to lie prone, shot him with whistling arrows more than a hundred times until clotted blood nearly weighed a stone, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He shot Yuan Ang more than a hundred times until he died in a mass of blood.

sentences.zh: 後帝自往弔，哭於喪次，逼擁其妻。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor went in person to mourn, wept at the mourning hall, and forced himself on his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Yuan Ang, wept at the bier, and forced his wife.

sentences.zh: 仍令從官脫衣助襚，兼錢綵，號為信物，一日所得，將踰巨萬。

translations.literal: He still ordered attendants to strip and assist in dressing the corpse, together with money and silks, called tokens of faith; in one day he gained more than a hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants stripped to dress the corpse; money and silks taken that day exceeded a hundred million.

sentences.zh: 后啼不食，乞讓位於姊，太后又為言，帝意乃釋。

translations.literal: The Empress wept and would not eat, begging to yield her place to her sister; the Empress Dowager also spoke for her; the Emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress wept and begged to yield to her sister until the Empress Dowager intervened.

sentences.zh: 所幸薛嬪，其被寵愛，忽意其經與高岳私通，無故斬首，藏之於懷。

translations.literal: The favored Lady Xue—suddenly suspecting she had secretly been with Gao Yue, he beheaded her without cause and hid the head in his bosom.
translations.idiomatic: Favored Lady Xue he suspected of affair with Gao Yue, beheaded her, and hid the head.

sentences.zh: 於東山宴，勸酬始合，忽探出頭，投於柈上。

translations.literal: At a feast on the eastern hills, when toasts had just begun, he suddenly drew out the head and cast it on the platter.
translations.idiomatic: At an eastern-hill feast he drew out her head and cast it on the platter.

sentences.zh: 支解其屍，弄其29a96為琵琶。

translations.literal: He dismembered the corpse and made her thigh into a pipa.
translations.idiomatic: He dismembered her and made her thigh into a pipa.

sentences.zh: 一座驚怖，莫不喪膽。

translations.literal: The whole company was terrified; all lost their courage.
translations.idiomatic: The company was terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝方收取，對之流淚云：「佳人難再得，甚可惜也。

translations.literal: The Emperor then took it up, wept facing it, and said, "A fair woman is hard to meet again—most pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: He wept over it: "A fair woman is hard to meet again."

sentences.zh: 」載屍以出，被髮步哭而隨之。

translations.literal: He carried the corpse out, hair loose, walking and weeping as he followed.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the corpse out, weeping as he walked.

sentences.zh: 至有閭巷庸猥，人無識知者，忽令召斬鄴下。

translations.literal: Even to vulgar fellows in lanes whom none knew, he suddenly ordered summoned and beheaded below Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded unknown commoners in the lanes of Ye.

sentences.zh: 繫徒罪至大辟，簡取隨駕，號為供御囚，手自刃殺，持以為戲。

translations.literal: Prisoners condemned to capital crimes were selected to follow the carriage as "imperial supply prisoners"; he personally bladed them for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners followed the carriage; he killed them for sport.

sentences.zh: 凡所屠害，動多支解，或投之烈火，或棄之漳流。

translations.literal: Of those he slaughtered, most were dismembered, cast into fire, or thrown into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Most victims were dismembered, burned, or thrown in the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 兼以外築長城，內營臺殿，賞費過度，天下騷然，內外憯憯，各懷怨毒。

translations.literal: Meanwhile he built the Long Wall outside and terraces and halls within; rewards and expenses were excessive; the realm was unsettled; within and without all were fearful, each nursing hatred.
translations.idiomatic: He built walls and halls at ruinous cost; the realm groaned under fear and hatred.

sentences.zh: 而素嚴斷臨下，加之默識強記，百僚戰慄，不敢為非。

translations.literal: Yet he was stern and decisive toward subordinates; added to keen silent memory, the hundred officials trembled in battle and dared not do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials trembled before his stern memory and dared not err.

sentences.zh: 曾有典御丞李集面諫，比帝有甚於桀紂。

translations.literal: Palace Provisioner Li Ji once remonstrated to his face that the Emperor surpassed Jie and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji said the Emperor surpassed Jie and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 帝令縳置流中，沈沒久之，復令引出，謂曰：「吾何如桀紂？

translations.literal: The Emperor had him bound and placed in the current, submerged a long time, then had him pulled out and said, "How am I compared to Jie and Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: He bound Li Ji, drowned him, pulled him out, and asked how he compared to Jie and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」集曰：「向來彌不及矣。

translations.literal: Ji said, "Just now you were even less than they."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Just now you were worse."

sentences.zh: 」帝又令沈之，引出更問，如此數四，集對如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor had him submerged again, pulled out and asked again; thus several times; Ji answered as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned and asked again several times; Ji answered the same.

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「天下有如此癡漢！

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and said, "Under heaven there is such a fool! Now I know Longfeng and Bigan were no wise men."
translations.idiomatic: He laughed: "Such a fool! Longfeng and Bigan were no sages."

sentences.zh: 方知龍逢、比干，非是俊物。

translations.literal: He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He released him.

sentences.zh: 」遂解放之。

translations.literal: Then he was brought in again to audience; seeming to remonstrate again, the Emperor ordered him taken out and cut at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Brought in again to remonstrate, he was cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 又被引入見，似有所諫，帝令將出腰斬。

translations.literal: Whether beheading or pardon—none could measure it.
translations.idiomatic: Beheading or pardon—none could predict.

sentences.zh: 其或斬或赦，莫能測焉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first ascended the throne he changed the era name to Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement he changed the era to Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 初帝登阼，改年為天保。

translations.literal: Men of deep insight said, "The characters for Tianbao form one great man plus ten—the Emperor will not pass ten?"
translations.idiomatic: Sages said Tianbao means one great man plus ten—he would not reign ten years?

sentences.zh: 士有深識者曰：「天保之字，為一大人只十，帝其不過十乎。

translations.literal: Men of deep insight said, "The characters for Tianbao form one great man plus ten—the Emperor will not pass ten?"
translations.idiomatic: Sages said Tianbao means one great man plus ten—he would not reign ten years?

sentences.zh: 」又先是謠云：「馬子入石室，三千六百日。

translations.literal: Earlier a rhyme said, "The horse-son enters the stone chamber—3,600 days."
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme said: "The horse-son enters the stone chamber—3,600 days."

sentences.zh: 」帝以午年生，故曰「馬子」；

translations.literal: The Emperor was born in a wu year; hence "horse-son";
translations.idiomatic: Born in a wu year, he was the horse-son;

sentences.zh: 三臺，石季龍舊居，故曰「石室」；

translations.literal: the Three Terraces were Shi Le's old residence; hence "stone chamber";
translations.idiomatic: the Three Terraces were Shi Le's residence—the stone chamber;

sentences.zh: 三千六百日，十年也。

translations.literal: 3,600 days is ten years.
translations.idiomatic: 3,600 days is ten years.

sentences.zh: 又帝曾問太山道士曰：「吾得幾年為天子？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked a Mount Tai daoist, "How many years shall I be Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked a Mount Tai daoist how many years he would reign.

sentences.zh: 」荅曰：「得三十年。

translations.literal: He answered, "Thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: The daoist said thirty years.

sentences.zh: 」道士出後，帝謂李后曰：「十年十月十日，得非三十也？

translations.literal: After the daoist left the Emperor told Empress Li, "Ten years, ten months, and ten days—is that not thirty?"
translations.idiomatic: After the daoist left he told Empress Li: ten years, ten months, and ten days—is that not thirty?

sentences.zh: 吾其畏之，過此無慮。

translations.literal: "I dread that date; beyond it I need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: He dreaded that date; beyond it he need not worry.

sentences.zh: 人生有死，何得致惜，但憐正道尚幼，人將奪之耳。

translations.literal: "Life must end—why grieve? Only Zhengdao is still young; others will seize him."
translations.idiomatic: Life must end—why grieve? Only young Zhengdao worried him.

sentences.zh: 」帝及期而崩，濟南竟不終位，時以為知命。

translations.literal: The Emperor died on schedule; Prince of Jinan did not finish his reign; men then said he knew fate.
translations.idiomatic: He died on schedule; Jinan did not finish his reign—men said he knew fate.

sentences.zh: 曾幸晉陽，夜宿杠門嶺。

translations.literal: Once visiting Jinyang he lodged overnight at Gangmen Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Jinyang he lodged at Gangmen Ridge.

sentences.zh: 嶺有數株柏樹，皆將千年，枝葉嫩茂，似有神物所託。

translations.literal: Several cypress trees on the ridge were nearly a thousand years old, branches and leaves tender and lush, as if possessed by a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient cypresses on the ridge seemed spirit-haunted.

sentences.zh: 時帝已被酒，向嶺瞋罵，射中一株，未幾，立枯而死。

translations.literal: The Emperor was already drunk; facing the ridge he cursed and shot one tree; before long it withered and died standing.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he cursed the ridge and shot a cypress; it withered at once.

sentences.zh: 又出言屢中，時人故謂之神靈。

translations.literal: His words also often hit true; men therefore called him numinous.
translations.idiomatic: His words often came true; men called him numinous.

sentences.zh: 雖為猖獗，不專云昏暴。

translations.literal: Though rampant he was not wholly called muddled and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Though wild he was not wholly mindless.

sentences.zh: 末年遂不能進食，唯數飲酒，麴糱成災，因而致斃。

translations.literal: In his last years he could no longer eat, drinking only wine; yeast became calamity and thus he died.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he drank only wine until yeast poison killed him.

sentences.zh: 先是，霍州發楚夷王女冢，尸如生焉，得珠襦玉匣，帝珍之，還以歛焉。

translations.literal: Earlier at Huo Province the tomb of the Chu king's daughter was opened; the corpse was as if alive; pearl jacket and jade casket were obtained; the Emperor treasured them and reclothed her in them.
translations.idiomatic: Opening a Chu princess tomb he found the corpse fresh and reclothed it in her treasures.

sentences.zh: 始祖珽以險薄多過，帝數罪之，每謂為老賊。

translations.literal: Progenitor Ting was treacherous and thin with many faults; the Emperor often condemned him, calling him old thief.
translations.idiomatic: Progenitor Ting he often called old thief for his treachery.

sentences.zh: 及武成時，珽被任遇，乃說武成曰：「文宣甚暴，何得稱文？

translations.literal: Under Wucheng, Ting was favored; he told Wucheng, "Wenxuan was very violent—how can he be called Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: Ting told Wucheng Wenxuan was too violent to be called Wen.

sentences.zh: 旣非創業，何得稱祖？

translations.literal: "He did not found the enterprise—how can he be called Progenitor?"
translations.idiomatic: He did not found the enterprise—how could he be called Progenitor?

sentences.zh: 若宣帝為祖，陛下萬歲後將何以稱？

translations.literal: "If Emperor Xuan is progenitor, what will Your Majesty be called after ten thousand years?"
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan is progenitor, what title would Wucheng bear after death?

sentences.zh: 」武成溺於珽說，天統初，有詔改謚景烈，廟號威宗。

translations.literal: Wucheng drowned in Ting's words; in the first year of Tiantong an edict changed the posthumous title to Jinglie and temple name Weizong.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng changed his posthumous title to Jinglie and temple name Weizong.

sentences.zh: 武平初，趙彥深執政，又奏復帝本謚，廟號顯祖云。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping, Zhao Yanshen held power and again memorialized restoration of the original posthumous title and temple name Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen restored the original posthumous title and temple name Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 廢帝殷字正道，小名道人，文宣帝之長子也。

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Yin, courtesy name Zhengdao, small name Daoren, was Wenxuan's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Yin, style Zhengdao, nickname Daoren, was Wenxuan's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰李皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Li.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Li.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，立為皇太子，時年六歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was installed crown prince at age six.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year one he became crown prince at six.

sentences.zh: 性敏慧，初學反語，於迹字下注云「自反」。

translations.literal: Clever and quick-witted, when first learning fanqie he wrote beneath the character ji "self-reflecting."
translations.idiomatic: Clever in fanqie, he wrote "self-reflecting" under the character ji.

sentences.zh: 時侍者未達其故，太子曰：「迹字足傍亦為迹，豈非自反邪。

translations.literal: Attendants did not understand; the crown prince said, "The character ji with foot beside is also ji—is that not self-reflecting?"
translations.idiomatic: He explained ji with foot beside is self-reflecting.

sentences.zh: 」嘗宴北宮，獨令河間王勿入，左右問其故，太子曰：「世宗遇賊處，河間王復何宜在此。

translations.literal: Once feasting at the Northern Palace he alone excluded the Prince of Hejian; asked why, the crown prince said, "Where Shizong met assassins—what place has the Prince of Hejian here?"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast he excluded Prince of Hejian because assassins had struck there.

sentences.zh: 」文宣每言「太子得漢家性質，不似我」，欲廢之，立太原王。

translations.literal: Wenxuan often said, "The crown prince has Han nature, not like me," and wished to depose him and install the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan said the crown prince was Han-like, not like him, and wished to replace him with Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初詔國子博士李寶鼎傅之，寶鼎卒，復詔國子博士邢峙侍講。

translations.literal: At first an edict made National University Doctor Li Baoding his tutor; when Baoding died, Doctor Xing Zhi was ordered to attend and lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoding then Xing Zhi tutored him.

sentences.zh: 太子雖富於春秋，而溫裕開朗，有人君之度，貫綜經業，省覽時政，甚有美名。

translations.literal: Though young in years the crown prince was warm, generous, and open, with the measure of a ruler; he mastered the classics and reviewed current affairs, winning great praise.
translations.idiomatic: Young yet open and kingly, he mastered classics and affairs and won praise.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，文宣召朝臣文學者及禮學官於宮宴會，令以經義相質，親自臨聽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Wenxuan summoned literary courtiers and ritual officials to a palace feast, had them debate classic meaning, and listened in person.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Wenxuan had scholars debate classics at a palace feast.

sentences.zh: 太子手筆措問，在坐莫不歎美。

translations.literal: The crown prince wrote questions by hand; those seated all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's written questions won admiration.

sentences.zh: 九年，文宣在晉陽，太子監國，集諸儒講孝經，令楊愔傳旨謂國子助教許散愁曰「先生在世，何以自資？

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wenxuan was at Jinyang; the crown prince oversaw the state, gathered Confucians to lecture the Classic of Filial Piety, and had Yang Yin convey the question to National University Assistant Instructor Xu San'chou, "How do you support yourself in the world, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he oversaw the state and asked Xu San'chou how he supported himself.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「散愁自少以來，不登孌童之牀，不入季女之室，服膺簡策，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: He answered, "Since youth I have not mounted the bed of pretty boys nor entered maidens' chambers; I embrace books and know not that old age comes.
translations.idiomatic: San'chou said he never entered boys' beds or maidens' chambers and lived by books.

sentences.zh: 平生素懷，若斯而已。

translations.literal: My lifelong intent is only this."
translations.idiomatic: His lifelong intent was only this.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「顏子縮屋稱貞，柳下嫗而不亂，未若此翁白首不娶者也。

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Yanzi lived in a shrunken house and was called chaste; Liuxia kept a concubine without disorder—not like this old man white-haired and unmarried."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince praised his lifelong celibacy over Yanzi and Liuxia.

sentences.zh: 」及賚絹百疋。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He received a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後文宣登金鳳臺，召太子使手刃囚。

translations.literal: Later Wenxuan ascended the Golden Phoenix Terrace and summoned the crown prince to personally behead a prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan summoned him to behead a prisoner on Golden Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 太子惻然有難色，再三不斷其首。

translations.literal: The crown prince looked pained and had difficulty; thrice he could not sever the head.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince could not bring himself to strike thrice.

sentences.zh: 文宣怒，親以馬鞭撞太子三下。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was angry and personally struck the crown prince three times with a horsewhip.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan horsewhipped him three times.

sentences.zh: 由是氣悸語吃，精神時復昏擾。

translations.literal: From this he had palpitations, stammering speech, and spirits sometimes disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He developed palpitations, stammer, and mental disturbance.

sentences.zh: 十年十月，文宣崩，癸卯，太子即帝位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，內外百官普加汎級，亡官失爵，聽復資品。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year Wenxuan died; on guimao the crown prince took the throne at Xuande Hall in Jinyang, proclaimed general amnesty, and all officials within and without were broadly advanced in rank; lost office and fief could be restored.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao after Wenxuan died he ascended at Jinyang, pardoned the realm, and restored ranks.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，尊皇太后為太皇太后，皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the empresses were raised in title.

sentences.zh: 詔九州軍人七十已上，授以板職；

translations.literal: An edict granted official rank to soldiers of the nine provinces seventy and above;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers seventy and above received rank;

sentences.zh: 武官年六十已上，及癃病不堪驅使者，並皆放免；

translations.literal: military officers sixty and above and those crippled or too ill for service were all released;
translations.idiomatic: officers sixty and above and the crippled were released;

sentences.zh: 土木營造金銅鐵諸雜作工，一切停罷。

translations.literal: earthwork, metal, copper, iron, and all miscellaneous crafts were entirely halted.
translations.idiomatic: all construction and metal crafts halted.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，以右丞相、咸陽王斛律金為左丞相，以錄尚書事、常山王演為太傅，以司徒、長廣王湛為太尉，以司空段韶為司徒，以平陽王淹為司空，高陽王湜為尚書左僕射，河間王孝琬為司州牧，侍中燕子獻為右僕射。

translations.literal: On yimao Right Chancellor Prince of Xianyang Hulu Jin was made Left Chancellor; Recorder Prince of Changshan Yan was made Grand Tutor; Minister of Works Prince of Changgang Zhan was made Grand Commandant; Minister of Works Duan Shao was made Minister of Works; Prince of Pingyang Yan was made Minister of Works; Prince of Gaoyang Shi was made Left Vice Minister; Prince of Hejian Xiaowan was made Governor of Si Province; Palace Attendant Yan Zixian was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were reshuffled: Hulu Jin, Yan, Zhan, Duan Shao, and others.

sentences.zh: 戊午，分命使者，巡省四方，求政得失，省察風俗，問人疾苦。

translations.literal: On wuwu envoys were dispatched separately to tour the four quarters, seek governmental gains and losses, observe customs, and inquire into hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu envoys toured the realm for policy and hardship.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，改封上黨王紹仁為漁陽王，廣陽王紹義為范陽王，長樂王紹廉為隴西王。

translations.literal: On wuxu Prince of Shangdang Shaoren was changed to Prince of Yuyang, Prince of Guangyang Shaoyi to Prince of Fanyang, Prince of Changle Shaolian to Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu three princes were re-enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周武成元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Wucheng of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Zhou Wucheng year one.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。

translations.literal: On yisi Grand Preceptor Prince of Changshan Yan by forged edict executed Director Yang Yin, Right Vice Minister Yan Zixian, Commander of the Guard Kezhuhun Tianhe, Palace Attendant Song Qindao, and Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Prince of Changshan Yan forged an edict and executed Yang Yin and four others.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以常山王演為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛為太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶為大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹為太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥為司徒，彭城王浟為尚書令。

translations.literal: On wushen Prince of Changshan Yan was made Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Recorder; Grand Marshal Prince of Changgang Zhan was made Grand Tutor and Grand Commander of the Capital Region; Minister of Works Duan Shao was made Grand General; former Minister of Works Prince of Pingyang Yan was made Grand Commandant; Minister of Works Prince of Pingqin Guiyan was made Minister of Works; Prince of Pengcheng You was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies, and recorder of the masters of writing; Grand Marshal Prince Zhan of Changgang became grand tutor and metropolitan commander; Minister of Works Duan Shao became grand general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, became grand commandant; Minister of Works Prince Guiyan of Pingqin became minister of works; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 又以高麗王世子湯為使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。

translations.literal: Goguryeo king's heir Tang was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo heir Tang received kingly titles.

sentences.zh: 是月，王琳為陳所敗，蕭莊自拔至和州。

translations.literal: That month Wang Lin was defeated by Chen; Xiao Zhuang escaped alone to He Province.
translations.idiomatic: That month Chen defeated Wang Lin; Xiao Zhuang fled to He Province.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，詔軍國事皆申晉陽，稟大丞相常山王規筭。

translations.literal: On jiayin of the third month an edict said all military and state affairs were to be reported to Jinyang and decided by Grand Chancellor Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin military affairs were referred to Prince of Changshan at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，封文襄第二子孝珩為廣寧王，第三子長恭為蘭陵王。

translations.literal: On renshen Wenxiang's second son Xiaohang was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning and third son Changgong as Prince of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Xiaohang and Changgong were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸亥，詔河南定、冀、趙、瀛、滄、南膠、光、南青九州，往因螽水，頗傷時稼，遣使分塗贍恤。

translations.literal: On guihai of the fourth month an edict sent envoys to nine provinces harmed by locusts and flood to relieve and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai nine provinces struck by locust and flood received relief.

sentences.zh: 是月，周明帝崩。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Ming of Zhou died.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhou's Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子，以開府儀同三司劉洪徽為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On renzi Regular Attendant Liu Honghui was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Liu Honghui became Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 秋八月壬午，太皇太后令廢帝為濟南王，全食一郡，以大丞相、常山王演入纂大統。

translations.literal: On renwu the Grand Empress Dowager ordered the Deposed Emperor made Prince of Jinan with a full commandery as fief; Grand Chancellor Prince of Changshan Yan entered to succeed the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Deposed Emperor became Prince of Jinan; Yan succeeded the throne.

sentences.zh: 是日，王居別宮。

translations.literal: That day the prince dwelt in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day he moved to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年九月，殂於晉陽，時年十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Huangjian year two he died at Jinyang at age seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangjian year two, ninth month, he died at Jinyang at seventeen.

sentences.zh: 初，文宣命邢卲制帝名殷字正道，從而尤之，曰：「殷家弟及，『正』字一止，吾身後兒不得也。

translations.literal: At first Wenxuan had Xing Shao compose the name Yin and style Zhengdao; he then especially faulted it, saying, "The Yin house succeeds younger brothers; the character zheng has one stop—I shall have no son after me."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan faulted the name Yin and style Zhengdao: "Yin succeeds younger brothers; zheng has one stop—no son after me."

sentences.zh: 」卲懼，請改焉。

translations.literal: Shao feared and requested change.
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked to change it.

sentences.zh: 文宣不許，曰：「天也。

translations.literal: Wenxuan would not permit and said, "Heaven's will."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan refused: "Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 」因謂昭帝曰：「奪時但奪，慎勿殺也。」

translations.literal: He therefore told Emperor Xiao, "When you seize the throne seize it—take care not to kill."
translations.idiomatic: He told Emperor Xiao: "Seize power but do not kill."

sentences.zh: 孝昭帝

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao.

sentences.zh: 孝昭皇帝演字延安，神武皇帝弟六子，文宣皇帝之母弟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, courtesy name Yan'an, was Shenwu's sixth son and Wenxuan's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, style Yan'an, was Shenwu's sixth son and Wenxuan's full brother.

sentences.zh: 幼而英峙，早有大成之量，武明皇太后早所愛重。

translations.literal: In youth he towered in talent and early had the measure of great completion; Empress Dowager Wuming loved and valued him from early on.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed great promise; Empress Dowager Wuming loved him early.

sentences.zh: 魏元象元年，封常山郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang of Wei he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Yuanxiang year one he received Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及文襄執政，遣中書侍郎李同軌就霸府為諸弟師。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang held government he sent Palace Gentleman Li Tonggui to the hegemonic office as teacher to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang sent Li Tonggui to teach the princes.

sentences.zh: 帝所覽文籍，源其指歸，而不好辭彩。

translations.literal: Texts the Emperor read—he traced them to their intent and did not love verbal ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He read for intent, not ornament.

sentences.zh: 每歎云：「雖盟津之師左驂震而不衂」，以為能。

translations.literal: He often sighed, "Though at Meng Ford the left outer horse trembled yet did not bleed," taking that as ability.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the left horse at Meng Ford that trembled but did not bleed.

sentences.zh: 遂篤志讀漢書，至李陵傳，恒壯其所為焉。

translations.literal: He then devoted himself to reading the Book of Han; at the biography of Li Ling he always admired Li Ling's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He read the Book of Han and admired Li Ling's conduct.

sentences.zh: 聦敏過人，所與游處，一知其家諱，終身未嘗誤犯。

translations.literal: Keenly intelligent beyond others, among those he associated with he knew each family's taboo names and never once erred in violation all his life.
translations.idiomatic: He knew every associate's taboo names and never once offended them.

sentences.zh: 同軌病卒，又命開府長流參軍刁柔代之，性嚴褊，不適誘訓之宜，中被遣出。

translations.literal: When Tonggui died of illness, he was ordered to appoint Chief Clerk of the Opening Office Diao Rou in his place; Rou was stern and narrow, unsuited to gentle instruction, and was mid-course dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Tonggui died, Diao Rou replaced him but was dismissed for harshness.

sentences.zh: 帝送出閤，慘然歛容，淚數行下，左右莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: The Emperor escorted him out the gate, his face somber and withdrawn, tears streaming down; attendants all wept softly.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted Rou out in tears while attendants wept.

sentences.zh: 其敬業重舊如此。

translations.literal: Such was his respect for teachers and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his respect for teachers and old friends.

sentences.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year one he was made a prince.

sentences.zh: 五年，除并省尚書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing for Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝善斷割，長思理，省內畏服。

translations.literal: The Emperor was skilled in deciding and cutting, long in deliberation; within the ministry all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He decided firmly and deliberated deeply; the ministry feared him.

sentences.zh: 七年，從文宣還鄴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Wenxuan back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he followed Wenxuan to Ye.

sentences.zh: 文宣以尚書奏事，多有異同，令帝與朝臣先論定得失，然後敷奏。

translations.literal: Wenxuan because memorials from the Masters of Writing often differed ordered the Emperor and court ministers first to debate gains and losses, then present memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan had him debate memorials with ministers before presentation.

sentences.zh: 帝長於政術，割斷咸盡其理，文宣歎重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor excelled in government, cutting and judging all to their principle; Wenxuan sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered policy; Wenxuan admired him.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉司空、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became Minister of Works and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 九年，除大司馬，仍錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Grand Marshal, still Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he became Grand Marshal and still Recorder.

sentences.zh: 時文宣溺於游宴，帝憂憤，表於神色。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan drowned in feasting and tours the Emperor showed worry and anger in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan's debauchery showed in the Emperor's worried face.

sentences.zh: 文宣覺之，謂帝曰：「但令汝在，我何為不縱樂？

translations.literal: Wenxuan noticed and said to the Emperor, "So long as you remain, why should I not indulge?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan said, "With you here, why should I not indulge?"

sentences.zh: 」帝唯啼泣拜伏，竟無所言。

translations.literal: The Emperor only wept and bowed, saying nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and bowed silently.

sentences.zh: 文宣亦大悲，抵盃於地曰：「汝似嫌我，自今敢進酒者斬之！

translations.literal: Wenxuan also grieved greatly, dashed cups to the ground, and said, "You seem to dislike me—from now on whoever dares advance wine—behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan smashed cups and forbade wine on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 」因取所御盃，盡皆壞棄。

translations.literal: He then took all cups he used and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed all his cups.

sentences.zh: 後益沈湎，或入諸貴戚家，角力批拉，不限貴賤。

translations.literal: Later he sank further into drink, or entered noble houses for wrestling and brawling without limit of noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: He drank deeper and wrestled in noble houses without distinction of rank.

sentences.zh: 唯常山王至，內外肅然。

translations.literal: Only when Prince of Changshan came was all within and without solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Changshan's arrival restored order.

sentences.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可，帝不從，因間極言，遂逢大怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor also secretly drafted articles of remonstrance; his friend Wang Xi thought it impossible but the Emperor did not listen; he remonstrated bluntly and met great anger.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted remonstrance against Wang Xi's advice and was furiously rebuked.

sentences.zh: 順成后本魏朝宗室，文宣欲帝離之，陰為帝廣求淑媛，望移其寵。

translations.literal: Empress Shuncheng was originally of Wei imperial clan; Wenxuan wished the Emperor to leave her and secretly sought fair ladies for him, hoping to shift his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan sought new consorts to shift the Emperor's favor from Empress Shuncheng.

sentences.zh: 帝雖承旨有納，而情義彌重。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor accepted as ordered he still loved her the more.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted consorts but loved the Empress more.

sentences.zh: 帝性頗嚴，尚書郎中剖斷有失，輒加捶楚，令史姦慝，便即考竟。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was quite stern; when Masters of Writing directors erred in judgment he added beating; when clerks were wicked he at once examined to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He beat erring directors and examined wicked clerks harshly.

sentences.zh: 文宣乃立帝於前，以刀環擬脅，召被帝罰者，臨以白刃，求帝之短，咸無所陳，方見解釋。

translations.literal: Wenxuan then stood the Emperor before him, threatened with blade ring, summoned those the Emperor had punished, held white blades to them, sought the Emperor's faults—all declared none, and then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan threatened those the Emperor punished until they cleared him.

sentences.zh: 自是不許笞箠郎中。

translations.literal: From this beating Masters of Writing directors was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Beating directors was forbidden thereafter.

sentences.zh: 後賜帝魏時宮人，醒而忘之，謂帝擅取，遂令刀環亂築，因此致困。

translations.literal: Later Wenxuan bestowed Wei palace women; waking he forgot and said the Emperor had taken them on his own; he ordered random beating with blade rings, thus causing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan forgot gifting palace women and beat him sick with blade rings.

sentences.zh: 皇太后日夜啼泣，文宣不知所為。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept day and night; Wenxuan knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wept; Wenxuan was helpless.

sentences.zh: 先是禁友王晞，乃捨之，令侍帝。

translations.literal: Earlier his friend Wang Xi had been forbidden; he now released him to attend the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He released Wang Xi to attend the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝月餘漸瘳，不敢復諫。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Emperor gradually recovered and dared not remonstrate again.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he recovered and dared not remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 及文宣崩，帝居禁中護喪事，幼主即位，乃即朝班。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan died the Emperor stayed within the palace guarding the mourning; when the young lord ascended he then took his place in court.
translations.idiomatic: He guarded Wenxuan's mourning then joined court when the young lord ascended.

sentences.zh: 除太傅、錄尚書事，朝政皆決於帝。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Tutor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing—all court governance was decided by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Tutor and Recorder he decided all governance.

sentences.zh: 月餘，乃居藩邸。

translations.literal: After more than a month he then dwelt at his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he returned to his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 自是，詔敕多不關帝。

translations.literal: From this edicts often did not pass through the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts often bypassed him.

sentences.zh: 客或言於帝曰：「鷙鳥捨巢，必有探卵之患，今日之地，何宜屢出。」

translations.literal: A guest said to the Emperor, "When the fierce bird leaves the nest there is the trouble of probing for eggs—what place is this to go out often today?"
translations.idiomatic: A guest warned: leaving the nest invites danger—why go out often?

sentences.zh: 三月甲戌，帝初上省，旦，發領軍府，大風暴起，壞所御車幔，帝甚惡之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu of the third month the Emperor first attended the ministry; at dawn leaving the Commander's office a great wind arose and destroyed his carriage curtains—he greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu going to the ministry a storm destroyed his carriage curtains—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及至省，朝士咸集。

translations.literal: When he reached the ministry courtiers all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry courtiers assembled.

sentences.zh: 坐定，酒數行，於坐執尚書令楊愔、右僕射燕子獻、領軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道等。

translations.literal: Seated, after several rounds of wine, he seized Director Yang Yin, Right Vice Minister Yan Zixian, Commander of the Guard Kezhuhun Tianhe, and Palace Attendant Song Qindao.
translations.idiomatic: After wine he seized Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, and Song Qindao.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服與平原王段韶、平秦王高歸彥、領軍劉洪徽入自雲龍門，於中書省前遇散騎常侍鄭子默，又執之，同斬於御府之內。

translations.literal: The Emperor in martial dress with Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao, Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, and Commander of the Guard Liu Honghui entered from Cloud Dragon Gate; at the front of the Masters of Writing he met Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo and seized and beheaded him together inside the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: In martial dress with Duan Shao, Guiyan, and Liu Honghui he entered and beheaded Zheng Zimo.

sentences.zh: 帝至東閤門，都督成休寧抽刃呵帝。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached the Eastern Gate; Commander Cheng Xiuning drew blade and shouted at the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Gate Cheng Xiuning drew blade and shouted.

sentences.zh: 帝令高歸彥喻之，休寧厲聲大呼不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Guiyan explain; Xiuning shouted loudly and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan tried to explain; Xiuning refused.

sentences.zh: 歸彥旣為領軍，素為兵士所服，悉皆弛仗，休寧方歎息而罷。

translations.literal: Guiyan being Commander of the Guard was long trusted by soldiers—all laid down arms; Xiuning then sighed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers obeyed Guiyan; Xiuning yielded.

sentences.zh: 帝入至昭陽殿，幼主、太皇太后、皇太后並出臨御坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor entered to Zhaoyang Hall; the young lord, Grand Empress Dowager, and Empress Dowager all came out to the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zhaoyang Hall; the empresses and young lord came out.

sentences.zh: 帝奏愔等罪，求伏專擅之辜。

translations.literal: The Emperor reported Yin and others' crimes and sought to confess exclusive usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the crimes of Yin and others.

sentences.zh: 時庭中及兩廊下衞士二千餘人，皆被甲待詔。

translations.literal: At the time in the court and both corridors more than two thousand guards wore armor awaiting edict.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand armored guards awaited edict.

sentences.zh: 武衞娥永樂武力絕倫，又被文宣重遇，撫刃思效。

translations.literal: Martial Guard E Yongle had peerless strength and was also favored by Wenxuan; he grasped blade intending loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: E Yongle, favored by Wenxuan, drew blade to act.

sentences.zh: 廢帝吃訥，兼倉卒，不知所言。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor stammered and in haste knew not what to say.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor stammered helplessly.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后又為皇太后誓，言帝無異志，唯云逼而已。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager also swore for the Empress Dowager that the Emperor had no other intent—only said forced.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager swore he acted only under force.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥敕勞衞士解嚴，永樂乃內刀而泣。

translations.literal: Guiyan ordered the guards to stand down; Yongle sheathed blade and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan stood down the guards; Yongle wept and sheathed his blade.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令歸彥引侍衞之士向華林園，以京畿軍入守門閤，斬娥永樂於園。

translations.literal: The Emperor then had Guiyan lead attendant guards to Hualin Garden, sent capital-region troops to guard gates, and beheaded E Yongle in the garden.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yongle beheaded in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 詔以帝為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，相府佐史進位一等。

translations.literal: An edict made the Emperor Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Recorder; staff of the chancellor's office advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Chancellor; staff advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 帝尋如晉陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 有詔，軍國大政，咸諮決焉。

translations.literal: An edict: all great military and state affairs were to be consulted and decided.
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs were referred to him.

sentences.zh: 帝旣當大位，知無不為，擇其令典，考綜名實，廢帝恭己以聽政。

translations.literal: Once he held the great position he left nothing undone, chose good models, examined names and reality; the Deposed Emperor deferentially listened to governance.
translations.idiomatic: He governed fully while the Deposed Emperor deferentially listened.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后尋下令廢少主，命帝統大業。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager soon ordered the young lord deposed and commanded the Emperor to inherit the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager deposed the young lord and made him emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔分遣大使，巡省四方，觀察風俗，問人疾苦，考求得失，搜訪賢良。
