translations.literal: On renchen an edict dispatched great envoys separately to tour the four quarters, observe customs, inquire into hardships, examine gains and losses, and seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen envoys toured the realm seeking worthies and hardships.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「昔武王剋殷，先封往代，兩漢魏晉，無廢茲典。

translations.literal: On jiawu an edict said, "Formerly King Wu overcame Yin and first enfeoffed former dynasties; Han, Wei, and Jin did not abolish this canon.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he ordered debate on enfeoffing former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 及元氏統歷，不率舊章；

translations.literal: When the Yuan house held the throne they did not follow old statutes;
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan house had not followed old statutes;

sentences.zh: 朕纂承大業，思弘古典。

translations.literal: I inherit the great enterprise and think to expand the ancient canon.
translations.idiomatic: he sought to expand the ancient canon.

sentences.zh: 但二王三恪，舊說不同，可議定是非，列名條奏。

translations.literal: But the two kings and three respects have old explanations that differ—debate right and wrong and list names in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered debate on the two kings and three respects.

sentences.zh: 其禮儀體式，亦仰議之。

translations.literal: Their ritual forms also submit for debate."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual forms were also submitted for debate.

sentences.zh: 」又詔國子寺可備立官屬，依舊置生，講習經典，歲時考試。

translations.literal: Another edict: the Directorate of the Sons of the State should prepare official posts, establish students as before, lecture classics, and examine yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Students were restored at the Directorate with yearly exams.

sentences.zh: 其文襄帝所運石經，宜即施列於學館。

translations.literal: The stone classics Wenxiang transported should be set in order at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang's stone classics were set in the academy.

sentences.zh: 外州大學，亦仰典司，勤加督課。

translations.literal: Outer provincial great schools also relied on the responsible office for diligent supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial schools were supervised diligently.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔九州勳人有重封者，聽分授子弟，以廣骨肉之恩。

translations.literal: On bingshen an edict: meritorious men of the nine provinces with double fiefs might grant shares to sons and younger brothers to broaden kinship grace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen double fiefs could be shared with kin.

sentences.zh: 九月壬申，詔議定三祖樂。

translations.literal: On renshen of the ninth month an edict ordered deliberation on music for the three progenitors.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen music for the three progenitors was ordered.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月辛亥，立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為皇太子，賜天下為父後者，爵一級。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Consort Yuan was installed empress; heir Bainian was installed crown prince; all who were fathers received one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Empress Yuan and Crown Prince Bainian were installed; fathers received rank.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，有司奏太祖獻武皇帝廟宜奏武德之樂，舞昭烈之舞；

translations.literal: On guichou the officials memorialized: Grand Ancestor Emperor Xianwu's temple should perform Wude music and Zhaolie dance;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou temples were assigned music and dance;

sentences.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝廟宜奏文德之樂，舞宣政之舞；

translations.literal: Shizu Emperor Wenxiang's temple should perform Wende music and Xuanzheng dance;
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang's temple Wende and Xuanzheng;

sentences.zh: 高祖文宣皇帝廟宜奏文正之樂，舞光大之舞。

translations.literal: Gaozu Emperor Wenxuan's temple should perform Wenzheng music and Guangda dance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan's temple Wenzheng and Guangda.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 」庚申，詔以故太師尉景、故太師竇泰、故太師太原王婁昭、故太宰章武王厙狄干、故太尉段榮、故太師万俟普、故司徒蔡雋、故太師高乾、故司徒莫多婁貸文、故太保劉貴、故太保封祖裔、故廣州刺史王懷十三人配饗太祖廟庭，故太師清河王岳、故太宰安德王韓軌、故太宰扶風王可朱渾道元、故太師高昂、故大司馬劉豐、故太師万俟受洛干、故太尉慕容紹宗十一人配饗世宗廟庭，故太尉河東王潘相樂、故司空薛脩義、故太傅破六韓常三人配饗高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: On gengshen an edict enfeoffed in the Grand Ancestor's temple courtyard thirteen men including the late Grand Preceptor Wei Jing, Dou Tai, Prince of Taiyuan Lou Zhao, Grand Mentor Prince of Zhangwu Kudie Gan, Grand Commandant Duan Rong, Grand Preceptor Wan Qipu, Minister of Works Cai Jun, Grand Preceptor Gao Gan, Minister of Works Moduolou Daiwen, Grand Mentor Liu Gui, Grand Mentor Feng Zuyi, and Inspector of Guang Province Wang Huai; in Shizu's temple courtyard eleven men including Prince of Qinghe Yue, Prince of Ande Han Gui, Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Daoyuan, Gao Ang, Liu Feng, Wan Qishouluogan, and Murong Shaozong; in Gaozu's temple courtyard three men: Prince of Hedong Pan Xiangyue, Xue Xiuyi, and Poluhan Chang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict assigned thirteen late ministers—including Wei Jing, Dou Tai, Lou Zhao prince of Taiyuan, Kudie Gan prince of Zhangwu, Duan Rong, Wan Qipu, Cai Jun, Gao Gan, Moduolou Daiwen, Liu Gui, Feng Zuyi, and Wang Huai of Guangzhou—to share sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple court; eleven others—including Prince Yue of Qinghe, Prince Gui of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan prince of Fufeng, Gao Ang, Liu Feng, Wan Qishouluogan, and Murong Shaozong—in Shizong's temple court; and three more—Prince Pan Xiangyue of Hedong, Xue Xiuyi, and Poluhan Chang—in Gaozu's temple court.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝親戎北討庫莫奚，出長城。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor personally took the field north against Kumo Xi and went beyond the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: That month he marched north against Kumo Xi beyond the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 虜奔遁，分兵致討，大獲牛馬，括總入晉陽宮。

translations.literal: The barbarians fled; troops were divided to pursue; cattle and horses were taken in great numbers and driven into Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians fled; cattle and horses filled Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙午，車駕至晉陽。

translations.literal: On bingwu of the twelfth month the imperial carriage reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛亥，祀圓丘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on xinhai, he sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, on xinhai, he sacrificed at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 壬子，禘於太廟。

translations.literal: On renzi he performed di at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he performed di at the temple.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔降罪人各有差。

translations.literal: On guichou an edict pardoned criminals each according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou criminals were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，詔內外執事之官從五品已上、及三府主簿錄事參軍、諸王文學、侍御史、廷尉三官、尚書郎中、中書舍人，每二年之內，各舉一人。

translations.literal: On dingchou an edict: officials within and without from fifth rank up and secretaries of the three offices, literary attendants of princes, attendant censors, tribunal officials, Masters of Writing directors, and Masters of Writing Gentlemen—each within two years recommend one man.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou officials were ordered to recommend talent every two years.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙子，以尚書令、彭城王浟為太保，長樂王尉粲為太尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on bingzi, Director Prince of Pengcheng You was made Grand Mentor and Prince of Changle Wei Can was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi You became Grand Mentor and Wei Can Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 己酉，野雉栖于前殿之庭。

translations.literal: On jiyou wild pheasants roosted in the front hall's courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou pheasants roosted in the front hall court.

sentences.zh: 帝聦敏有識度，深沈能斷，不可窺測。

translations.literal: The Emperor was keen, intelligent, and far-sighted, deep and decisive beyond fathoming.
translations.idiomatic: He was keen, deep, and unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，儀望風表，迥然獨秀。

translations.literal: Eight chi tall, waist ten arm-spans around, bearing and appearance outstanding alone in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, ten spans at the waist, singular in bearing.

sentences.zh: 自居臺省，留心政術，閑明簿領，吏所不逮。

translations.literal: Since dwelling in the ministry he attended to government, clear in ledgers—clerks could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministry he mastered ledgers beyond any clerk.

sentences.zh: 及正位宸居，彌所克勵，輕徭薄賦，勤恤人隱。

translations.literal: Once enthroned he strove the more, light corvée and taxes, diligently succoring the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Enthroned he lightened burdens and succored the people.

sentences.zh: 內無私寵，外收人物，雖后父，位亦特進無別。

translations.literal: Within no private favor; without he gathered men—though the empress's father, rank was only Special Advance without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: He favored no private kin; even the empress's father had no special rank.

sentences.zh: 日昃臨朝，務知人之善惡。

translations.literal: At sunset he held court, striving to know men's good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: He held court at sunset seeking men's true character.

sentences.zh: 每訪問左右，冀獲直言。

translations.literal: He often questioned attendants hoping to obtain blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned attendants hoping for blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 曾問舍人裴澤在外議論得失，澤率爾對曰：「陛下聦明至公，自可遠侔古昔，而有識之士，咸言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。

translations.literal: Once he asked Attendant Pei Ze's outside discussions of gains and losses; Ze bluntly answered, "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and can match antiquity from afar, yet men of insight all say you are too meticulous—an emperor's measure is not yet broad."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ze said he was fair but too meticulous for an emperor's measure.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said, "Truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: He smiled: "Truly as you say.

sentences.zh: 朕初臨萬機，慮不周悉，故致爾耳。

translations.literal: When I first faced the myriad affairs I feared not being thorough and thus became so.
translations.idiomatic: When I first faced myriad affairs I feared not being thorough.

sentences.zh: 此事安可久行，恐後又嫌疏漏。

translations.literal: This cannot long continue—later they will fault me for laxity."
translations.idiomatic: This cannot last—later they will fault laxity."

sentences.zh: 」澤因被寵遇。

translations.literal: Ze thereby received favored treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ze was favored.

sentences.zh: 其樂聞過也如此。

translations.literal: Such was his joy in hearing of faults.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his joy in hearing faults.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王叡與厙狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「須拔我同堂弟，顯安我親姑子，今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and Kudie Xi'an sat in attendance; the Emperor said, "I must praise my cousin Xi'an is my aunt's son—today in family rite we remove ministerial reverence; speak of my shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: He invited family criticism from Rui and Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 」顯安曰：「陛下多妄言。

translations.literal: Xi'an said, "Your Majesty speaks much falsely."
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an said, "Your Majesty speaks falsely."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「若何？

translations.literal: He said, "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked how.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下昔見文宣以馬鞭撻人，常以為非，而今行之，非妄言邪？

translations.literal: He answered, "Your Majesty formerly saw Wenxuan beat men with a horsewhip and thought it wrong, yet now you do it—is that not false speech?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an said he now horsewhipped men though he once condemned it.

sentences.zh: 」帝握其手謝之。

translations.literal: The Emperor grasped his hand and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped Xi'an's hand and apologized.

sentences.zh: 又使直言，對曰：「陛下太細，天子乃更似吏。

translations.literal: He again ordered blunt speech; Xi'an answered, "Your Majesty is too meticulous—a Son of Heaven is more like a clerk."
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an said he was too meticulous, more clerk than emperor.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕甚知之，然無法來久，將整之以至無為耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I know this well, yet long lawlessness must be corrected toward non-action."
translations.idiomatic: He said lawlessness required correction toward non-action.

sentences.zh: 」又問王晞，晞荅如顯安，皆從容受納。

translations.literal: He again asked Wang Xi; Xi answered as Xi'an—all were calmly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi answered likewise and was accepted.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，太后不豫，出居南宮，帝行不正履，容色貶悴，衣不解帶，殆將四旬。

translations.literal: Filial to the utmost—when the Empress Dowager was unwell he moved to the Southern Palace; he walked without proper stride, countenance wan, clothes unremoved for nearly forty days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager was ill he mourned at her gate for forty days.

sentences.zh: 殿去南宮五百餘步，雞鳴而去，辰時方還，來去徒行，不乘輿輦。

translations.literal: The hall was more than five hundred paces from the Southern Palace; at cockcrow he went, at chen hour returned, coming and going on foot without carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He walked five hundred paces to her at cockcrow daily.

sentences.zh: 太后所苦小增，便即寢伏閤外，食飲藥物，盡皆躬親。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager's illness worsened slightly he slept outside her curtain, personally attending food, drink, and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He slept outside her curtain and attended her medicine.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗心痛，不自堪忍，帝立侍帷前，以爪搯手心，血流出袖。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager once had heart pain unbearable, the Emperor stood attending before the curtain and dug his fingernails into his palm until blood flowed from his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: He dug his nails into his palm until blood soaked his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 友愛諸弟，無君臣之隔。

translations.literal: He loved his brothers with no barrier of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He loved his brothers without royal distance.

sentences.zh: 雄勇有謀。

translations.literal: Heroic and brave with stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was heroic and stratagem-minded.

sentences.zh: 于時國富兵強，將雪神武遺恨，意在頓駕平陽，為進取之策。

translations.literal: At the time the state was rich and armies strong; he wished to avenge Shenwu's remaining regret and intended to halt at Pingyang as a plan of advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and strong, he planned to avenge Shenwu at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 遠圖不遂，惜哉。

translations.literal: The far design was not achieved—pity.
translations.idiomatic: The design failed—pity.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與濟南約，不相害。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor and Jinan agreed not to harm each other.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jinan agreed not to harm each other.

sentences.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云「鄴城有天子氣」。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng garrisoned Ye, geomancers said Ye had Son of Heaven aura.
translations.idiomatic: Geomancers said Ye had imperial aura while he was at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝恐濟南復興，乃密行鴆毒。

translations.literal: Fearing Jinan's revival he secretly administered poison.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jinan he secretly poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 濟南不從，乃扼而殺之。

translations.literal: Jinan would not comply and was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan refused and was strangled.

sentences.zh: 後頗愧悔。

translations.literal: Later he was quite ashamed and regretful.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 初苦內熱，頻進湯散。

translations.literal: At first he suffered inner heat and repeatedly took decoctions.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered inner heat and took medicine.

sentences.zh: 時有尚書令史姓趙，於鄴見文宣從楊愔、燕子獻等西行，言相與復讎。

translations.literal: An Masters of Writing clerk surnamed Zhao at Ye saw Wenxuan going west with Yang Yin and Yan Zixian seeking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhao at Ye dreamed Wenxuan going west with Yin and Zixian for revenge.

sentences.zh: 帝在晉陽宮，與毛夫人亦見焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor at Jinyang Palace with Lady Mao also saw it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he and Lady Mao saw the same vision.

sentences.zh: 遂漸危篤，備禳厭之事，或煑油四灑，或持炬燒逐。

translations.literal: He gradually reached critical illness; exorcisms were prepared—oil boiled and sprinkled four ways, or torches held to burn and drive away.
translations.idiomatic: Critically ill, he tried exorcism with oil and fire.

sentences.zh: 諸厲方出殿梁，山騎棟上，歌呼自若，了無懼容。

translations.literal: When evil spirits left the hall beams mountain riders on the ridge sang and shouted as if nothing feared.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits on the beams sang without fear.

sentences.zh: 時有天狗下，乃於其所講武以厭之，有兔驚馬，帝墜而絕肋。

translations.literal: When the heaven-dog descended he held martial review there to suppress it; a rabbit startled the horse and the Emperor fell breaking a rib.
translations.idiomatic: A rabbit startled his horse and he broke a rib.

sentences.zh: 太后視疾，問濟南所在者三，帝不對。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager attended the illness and thrice asked where Jinan was; the Emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager thrice asked after Jinan; he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 太后怒曰：「殺去邪！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager angrily said, "Kill and gone!
translations.idiomatic: She said, "You killed him—

sentences.zh: 不用吾言，死其宜矣。

translations.literal: You would not heed my words—dying is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: you ignored my words—dying is fitting."

sentences.zh: 」臨終之際，唯扶服牀枕，叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: At the end he only clutched the bed and kowtowed begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Dying he clutched the bed and begged.

sentences.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with edict summoning Prince of Changgang to inherit the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Prince of Changgang to succeed.

sentences.zh: 又手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」

translations.literal: He also wrote by hand, "Place my wife and children in a good place—do not imitate those before."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Protect my wife and children—do not imitate your predecessors."

sentences.zh: 論曰：神武平定四方，威權在己，遷鄴之後，雖主祭有人，號令所加，政皆自出。

translations.literal: Commentary: Shenwu pacified the four quarters; authority was his own; after moving to Ye though sacrifices had a master, orders added were all his own.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Shenwu held all power; after Ye even rites were his to command.

sentences.zh: 文宣因循鴻業，內外協從，自朝及野，羣心屬望，東魏之地，舉國樂推，曾未期月，遂登宸極。

translations.literal: Wenxuan followed the great enterprise; within and without harmonized; from court to wild all hearts looked to him; Eastern Wei's lands with the whole state rejoicing pushed him—within a month he ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan inherited universal acclaim and swiftly took the throne.

sentences.zh: 始則存心政事，風化肅然，數年之間，朝野安乂。

translations.literal: At first he devoted heart to government; customs were stern; within several years court and country were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At first his rule brought peace within years.

sentences.zh: 其後縱酒肆欲，事極猖狂，昏邪殘暴，近代未有，饗國不永，實由斯疾。

translations.literal: Afterward he indulged wine and desire to the extreme of madness—muddled, wicked, cruel, and violent unmatched in recent ages; enjoying the state not long was truly from this sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Then debauchery and cruelty unmatched in ages shortened his reign.

sentences.zh: 濟南繼業，大革其弊，風教粲然，搢紳稱幸。

translations.literal: Jinan succeeded and greatly reformed its ills; customs were brilliant; gentry called themselves fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan reformed abuses and gentry rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衞主。

translations.literal: Assisting ministers though loyal could neither praise virtue nor harmonize kin, nor guard themselves with foresight or deeply plot to protect the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers could neither harmonize kin nor protect the ruler.

sentences.zh: 應斷不斷，自取其災。

translations.literal: What should be cut was not cut—they invited their own disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to act decisively invited disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君尋廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。

translations.literal: Ministers were executed and destroyed; the ruler soon was deposed and shamed—all from appointing unfit men.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers died and the ruler was shamed for unfit appointments.

sentences.zh: 孝昭早居臺閣，故事通明，人吏之間，無所不委。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao early dwelt in the ministry, clear in precedent, between men and clerks nothing was not entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao early mastered the ministry and all affairs.

sentences.zh: 文宣崩後，大革前弊，及臨尊極，留心更深，時人服其明而譏其細也。

translations.literal: After Wenxuan died he greatly reformed former ills; enthroned he attended deeper; men admired his clarity yet mocked his meticulousness.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed Wenxuan's ills yet was mocked for meticulousness.

sentences.zh: 情好稽古，率由禮度，將封先代之胤，且敦學校之風，徵召才賢，文武畢集。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity and followed ritual, about to enfeoff former dynasties' heirs and encourage schools, gathering talent civil and military.
translations.idiomatic: He sought ritual, schools, and talent.

sentences.zh: 于時周氏朝政，移於宰臣，主將相猜，不無危殆。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou's court shifted to the chancellor; lord and minister suspected each other—not without peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's court was perilous with shifting power.

sentences.zh: 乃眷關右，寔懷兼并之志。

translations.literal: He then looked to Guanxi with real intent to merge.
translations.idiomatic: He looked west with intent to merge.

sentences.zh: 經謀宏曠，諒近代之明主。

translations.literal: Plans were vast and bright—a clear ruler of recent ages.
translations.idiomatic: His plans marked him a ruler of recent ages.

sentences.zh: 而降年不永，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Yet years granted were not long—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet his years were short—why?

sentences.zh: 豈幽顯之塗，別有復報；

translations.literal: Are dark and bright paths separately repaid;
translations.idiomatic: Are dark and bright paths separately repaid;

sentences.zh: 將齊之基宇，止在於斯，帝欲大之，天不許也？

translations.literal: or is Qi's foundation only here—the Emperor wished to enlarge it but Heaven did not permit?
translations.idiomatic: or did Heaven forbid enlarging Qi's foundation?
